# Intake brief — Permanent Force Field should regenerate its reflect budget (AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P)

## Headline

A hold-full (permanent) Force Field spends its 3–10 reflections once and then
sits dim and inert for the rest of the run, so the permanent reward stops being
a reward. Give the bubble a level-resolved recharge so a spent reflection
returns over time — mirroring the Thorn Field recharge
(AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T) — with the dim bubble brightening back to the active look
as reflections return, driven once from the shared registry tick so the game
and every gym behave identically.

## Problem statement

`EffectsRegistry.tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` decrements `_forceFieldRemaining`
and nothing ever puts a reflection back: `_forceFieldRemaining` is only ever
assigned on collection (`applyCollect`), cleared on window expiry
(`_expireTimedEffect`) and cleared by `reset()`. A **permanent** (hold-full)
field therefore starts at its level-resolved budget and, once spent, stays at
zero for the whole run. After AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z made the spent bubble **dim
rather than vanish**, that permanent reward now visibly advertises "up but
inert" for the remainder of the run.

The Thorn Field solved the same "permanent reward goes inert" problem with a
level-resolved recharge clock advanced from the shared `EffectsRegistry.tick`
(AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T). The Force Field has no equivalent.

## Users

- **Players who take the hold-full "Force Field" reward** — they paid a full
  hold for a permanent upgrade and expect it to keep earning reflections.

User stories:

- As a player with a permanent Force Field, I want spent reflections to come
  back over time, so my hold-full reward keeps defending me instead of going
  quiet after three bounces.
- As a player, I want to see when the next reflection is due, so the dim bubble
  does not read as broken.
- As a player, I want the bubble to visibly return to its active look when a
  reflection comes back, so I can tell "recharging" from "dead".
- As a maintainer, I want the recharge to live once in the shared
  `EffectsRegistry` tick, so the game and every gym refill identically
  (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Recharge clock.** A new level-resolved interval puts one spent reflection
  back: `EffectsRegistry` exposes `forceFieldRechargeTime()`,
  `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()` and `forceFieldMaxReflects()` (the resolved
  `forceFieldReflects` budget), advanced **only** from the shared
  `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` (the single call site every scene already uses).
  One reflection returns per elapsed interval, a long frame returns exactly as
  many reflections as the elapsed time warrants (remainder carried, no
  banking), and the budget never exceeds `forceFieldMaxReflects()`.
- **Level axis.** A new `forceFieldRecharge` variable in
  `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.force_field` (descending linear-clamped interval, whole
  seconds) plus the derived, monotonic non-decreasing rate axis
  `forceFieldRechargeRate = 1 / interval`, mirroring `thornsRecharge` /
  `thornsRechargeRate`. Draft tuning: **12 s at level 0 → 5 s floor, −1 s per
  level** (see Open Question 1).
- **Scope.** Recharge runs while a Force Field is active — for the whole run on
  a permanent (hold-full) grant, and while its window is still open on a field
  pickup — up to the level-resolved budget. A spent budget on an inactive field
  never resurrects (window expiry and `reset()` clear the clock, exactly like
  the Thorn Field).
- **Visual follow-through.** The bubble returns from the AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z
  spent-dim look to the active look as soon as `forceFieldRemaining() > 0`, and
  dims again when it is spent — through the existing shared
  `drawForceFieldBubble` gate, with no per-scene branch.
- **HUD.** The `Force Field ×N` row gains the `next in Ns` recharge countdown
  while a reflection is owed (extending `HUD._powerUpRecharge`, the same path
  the Thorn Field and permanent Orbital Strike use) and otherwise renders as it
  does today.
- **Tests.** Unit tests cover: one reflection per interval; cap at the
  level-resolved budget; frame-rate independence (many small ticks vs one long
  tick); no recharge while the window is inactive (temporary expiry clears the
  clock); a permanent field recharging for the whole run; a stronger level
  recharging faster; `reset()` clearing the clock; `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()`
  reported only while a reflection is owed; and the dim → active bubble
  transition driven by the refilled budget.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The registry tick remains the only recharge driver, and
  the existing parity suites (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` plus the
  `GymPowerUpLeveling` readout) cover the new axis without a second code path.
- **Docs.** The GDD `force_field` row (§4.2) and the power-up level-variable
  table (§ around line 1205) describe the recharge; the power-up description
  copy in `src/powerups/types.ts` (surfaced in the hold-full choice/help)
  mentions the budget returning over time. All related documentation is
  updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
  relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **One shared code path.** No scene-specific recharge timers; the clock lives
  in `EffectsRegistry` and advances only from `tick`, which `CombatScene` /
  `CombatCoreScene` already call for both `PlayScene` and every gym.
- **Additive level axis only.** Do not change existing `forceFieldDuration` /
  `forceFieldReflects` base/cap values or behaviour; the new axis is additive
  and monotonic (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` is iterated by completeness and
  monotonicity tests, so it must be registered in catalogue order).
- **No new assets, cues or textures.** The recharge is a timer plus the
  existing two-state bubble look; no new sound, no new VFX module.
- **Balance guardrail.** Recharge must stay slow enough that a field is never
  permanent immunity — the resolved budget cap plus a multi-second interval is
  the bound, exactly as for the Thorn Field.
- **CHANGELOG.md is out of scope** (ship-skill release pipeline owns it).

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`): `_forceFieldRemaining` (declared
  `:379`, set from `stats.forceFieldReflects` in `applyCollect` `:595`, cleared
  by `reset()` `:788` and by `_expireTimedEffect` `:787`, decremented in
  `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect` `:922`). Accessors `isForceFieldActive()` `:855`,
  `forceFieldRemaining()` `:864`, `forceFieldRadius()` `:872`.
- `tick(dt)` `:721` is the single shared advance path; it already drives
  `_levelStore.tickRecharge(dt)` and `_advanceThornsRecharge(dt)` — the direct
  precedent for a `_advanceForceFieldRecharge(dt)` call placed alongside it.
- Thorn Field recharge model to mirror: `_thornsRechargeTimer` `:405`,
  clock start in `tryConsumeThornsRam()` `:1124`, `thornsMaxAbsorbs()` `:1140`,
  `thornsRechargeTime()` `:1156`, `thornsRechargeRemaining()` `:1169`,
  `_advanceThornsRecharge(dt)` `:1182` (carries the remainder in a `while` loop,
  clears the clock on a full budget or an inactive window).
- Level model (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`): `force_field` specs at `:753`
  (`forceFieldDuration` 8 → 18 s, `forceFieldReflects` 3 → 10);
  `thornsRecharge` spec at `:907` (12 → 5 s, `k = -1`, `discrete: true`) with the
  derived `thornsRechargeRate` computed in the resolver (`:1214`) — the template
  for the new axis and its derived rate.
- Visual: `drawForceFieldBubble` (`src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts:304`)
  already gates on `isForceFieldActive()` and switches to the spent alphas when
  `registry.forceFieldRemaining() <= 0` (`:354`), so a refilled budget restores
  the active look with no visual change — the AC only needs a test pinning it.
- HUD (`src/ui/HUD.ts`): `_powerUpStacks` returns `forceFieldRemaining()` (`:549`);
  `_powerUpRecharge` (`:575`) handles `thorns` and `strike` only — the Force
  Field case is the gap.
- Power-up copy (`src/powerups/types.ts:233`): "the field returns a limited
  number of shots before it stops reflecting" — no mention of a returning
  budget.

## Desired change

1. Add the `forceFieldRecharge` level axis (interval, descending) and derive
   `forceFieldRechargeRate`, registered in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` in
   catalogue order right after `forceFieldReflects`.
2. Add the Force Field recharge clock to `EffectsRegistry`: start it on the
   first spent reflection (keeping a running countdown, never banking time),
   advance it from `tick`, cap the refill at the resolved budget, clear it when
   the field is inactive or the budget is full, and clear it in `reset()`.
3. Surface `forceFieldMaxReflects()`, `forceFieldRechargeTime()` and
   `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()` for the HUD, tests and any future help copy.
4. Add the `force_field` case to `HUD._powerUpRecharge` so the row shows
   `next in Ns` while a reflection is owed.
5. Update the power-up description copy and the two GDD sections.
6. Tests as listed in the ACs, including the dim → active bubble transition.

**Key Files:**

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Add the `forceFieldRecharge` variable, its `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.force_field` entry (12 s → 5 s, `k = -1`, `discrete: true`, with a written balance rationale), the `forceFieldRecharge`/`forceFieldRechargeRate` stat fields and the derived rate in the resolver; register the variable in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` after `forceFieldReflects`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — Add `_forceFieldRechargeTimer` plus `forceFieldMaxReflects()`, `forceFieldRechargeTime()`, `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()` and `_advanceForceFieldRecharge(dt)`; start the clock in `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()`; call the advance from `tick()` beside `_advanceThornsRecharge`; clear the clock in `_expireTimedEffect` (force_field branch) and `reset()`.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Extend `_powerUpRecharge` with the `force_field` case mapping `forceFieldRechargeRemaining()` to the existing `next in Ns` label; update the doc comment that says only the Thorn Field recharges.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — Update the `force_field` `description` copy so the hold-full choice/help states the budget returns over time.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — No behaviour change expected; confirm (and comment) that the spent-dim gate reads the live `forceFieldRemaining()` so a refill restores the active look.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update the §4.2 `force_field` row and the power-up level-variable table row to describe the recharge and its draft tuning.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — Recharge unit tests (timing, cap, frame-rate independence, inactive-window clearing, permanent run-long recharge, stronger level, `reset()`, countdown reporting).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` — Axis tests: descending whole-second interval 12 → 5, derived rate `1 / interval` non-decreasing, existing Force Field axes unchanged.
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` — `next in Ns` countdown appears for a recharging Force Field and disappears when the budget is full.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts` — Pin the spent-dim → active bubble transition when the budget is refilled by the shared tick.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / `powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` — Extend the existing parity sweeps so the recharge is observed identically in the game and the gyms.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (recharge granularity).** One reflection returns per interval
  with the remainder carried (Thorn Field semantics), and the clock starts on
  the first spend rather than running continuously — a field re-collected at a
  full budget has no banked time. This bounds worst-case reflect throughput to
  `budget + elapsed / interval`.
- **Assumption (no idle bonus).** Recharge only runs while the field is
  active; an expired pickup window clears the clock (matching
  AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T) so a re-collection never inherits partial progress.
- **Risk — permanent immunity.** A short interval on a high-level field
  (10 reflections at 5 s) approaches continuous reflection. Mitigation: the
  interval floor plus the existing budget cap, and the rationale recorded beside
  the spec entry so the numbers cannot drift silently.
- **Risk — balance drift from a new axis.** Adding `forceFieldRecharge` changes
  the level-up offer surface and the "how strong is this power-up" model.
  Mitigation: additive-only axis, monotonic contract enforced by the existing
  catalogue tests and the recorded rationale.
- **Risk — HUD noise.** A countdown that persists at a full budget would read
  as a stalled timer. Mitigation: report `undefined` when nothing is owed,
  exactly like the Thorn Field.
- **Scope-creep guardrail.** A graduated (per-reflection brightness) bubble
  scale, a Force Field recharge sound or a per-level recharge VFX are **out of
  scope** — the AC needs only the binary spent/active look returning. Record
  such ideas as separate work items rather than widening this one.
- **Assumption (docs only).** No CHANGELOG entry is authored here; the release
  pipeline owns it.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14** — More forcefield feedback (parent; Q1 = dim when
  spent). Explicitly deferred regeneration to this item.
- **AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z** — Force Field bubble: permanent persistence +
  spent-dim (the dim state this item has to undo on refill).
- **AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T** — What does Field of Thorns do? The recharge
  precedent (level axis + shared-tick clock + HUD countdown) this item mirrors.
- **AH-0MV1BIX1W006XF95** — Gradius force field reflector (origin of
  `_forceFieldRemaining`, `forceFieldReflects` and the reflect seam).
- **AH-0MVRDMMYO002SC5V** — Bounce-point flash + `playForceFieldReflectSound`
  in the shared reflect branch (unchanged by this item).
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — Gym-parity principle in AGENTS.md (the rule the
  shared-tick requirement satisfies).
- **AH-0MVS2T5N30031SL5 / AH-0MVS2T40T006QL7H** — Orbital Strike visibility +
  `next in Ns` HUD countdown (the other consumer of `_powerUpRecharge`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.2 power-up table and the level-variable
  table; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (parity matrix rows for `GymPowerUpsCombat`,
  `GymPowerUpLeveling`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — Recharge tuning.** Should `forceFieldRecharge` mirror
  Thorn Field exactly (descending `linear-clamped`, 12 s at level 0 → 5 s floor,
  −1 s per level, whole seconds, plus the derived `forceFieldRechargeRate`
  axis)?
  - (a) Mirror Thorn Field: 12 s → 5 s, −1 s/level. **Recommended** — one
    recharge cadence to learn across both fields, and the interval is slow
    enough that a field stays a buff rather than immunity.
  - (b) Slower: 15 s → 6 s.
  - (c) Fixed constant interval, no new level axis (contradicts the "resolved
    from level" AC).
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer.** No answer yet; the brief is
    drafted against (a).
- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION) — Scope of the recharge.** Should a temporary field
  pickup also recharge while its window is open, or only the permanent
  (hold-full) grant?
  - (a) Both — recharge whenever a field is active, up to the level-resolved
    budget, exactly like the Thorn Field. **Recommended** — one code path, no
    permanent-only special case, and the window is short enough that it rarely
    yields more than one extra reflection.
  - (b) Permanent grants only; a pickup keeps its one-shot budget.
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer.** Brief drafted against (a).
- **Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — HUD countdown.** Should the `Force Field ×N` row show
  the `next in Ns` recharge countdown (as the Thorn Field and permanent
  Orbital Strike do)?
  - (a) Yes — show it while a reflection is owed. **Recommended** — a dim
    bubble with a bare `×0` label reads as broken; the countdown explains the
    wait and reuses the existing formatter.
  - (b) No — keep `×N` only; the bubble's dim/active state carries the signal.
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer.** Brief drafted against (a).
- **Q (automated) — Duplicate check.** `wl search "force field"` returned the
  completed force-field items listed under Related work; none of them
  implements a reflect-budget recharge, so no duplicate was found. Source:
  `wl search force field --json`, 2026-10-30.

## Context

The producer decided (2026-10-27) that AI Hell will NOT run the full test suite in the pre-push hook — the suite runs repeatedly during implementation via the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`). The committed `.githooks/pre-push` keeps its v2 behaviour (branch policy, context budget, `wl sync`); the item AH-0MVMA87GX0061KUQ was re-purposed as a decision record and closed.

## Future conflict to revisit

SorraAgents **SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1** (open) plans to make the framework v3 pre-push hook resolve `run_tests.py` local-then-global and ship v3 to every project via `scripts/install_pi.sh`, with an upgrade path that replaces installed hooks carrying an old unmodified framework revision marker (backup + report). AI Hell's current `.githooks/pre-push` is an unmodified framework v2 copy, so when that lands, `install_pi.sh` would likely replace it with the gated v3 hook — silently re-introducing a full-suite gate and reversing the decision.

## Desired change

When SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1 lands (or during its review), choose how to preserve the no-gate decision:

- (a) keep the hook locally modified (a deliberate deviation that `install_pi.sh` reports rather than overwrites);
- (b) default `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` in the installed hook;
- (c) accept the gate (reversing the decision).

Record the choice on this item and update any local documentation.

## Acceptance criteria

- When SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1's v3 hook / installer upgrade reaches AI Hell (or is reviewed as an SA item), this item's decision is actioned and the outcome recorded here.
- AI Hell's `.githooks/pre-push` does not silently gain a full-suite gate without an explicit producer decision.
- A comment on this item links the relevant SA commit/PR and states the chosen option.

# Docs: CSV write-safety patterns and test isolation

**Parent:** AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12

## Summary

Document the CSV write-safety model introduced by the parent item: plugin root semantics
and escape refusal, the store's test-mode registry-only guard, the happy-dom fetch-bridge
requirement, and the suite-run tracked-CSV guard. Update the existing docs entries that
describe the CSV endpoints and the config store save path so they match the new behaviour.

## User story

As a maintainer/test author, I want the safe patterns written down next to the code they
apply to, so a future change does not reintroduce a cross-checkout CSV write.

## Scope

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` and `README.md` wherever
  the `/api/csv/...` endpoints, dev write-back or test patterns are described — update to
  state the root-isolation and test-mode guard behaviour (keep edits surgical; these are
  large docs, change only the relevant sections).
- Code comments where the behaviour lives: `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` (root
  semantics, why reads are guarded too), `src/core/configStore.ts` (test-mode save
  contract), `src/test/setup.ts` (default CSV fetch guard) and the new guard test module.
- Where a doc needs a home that does not exist yet, add a short section to the closest
  existing doc rather than creating a new top-level file.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Parent AC 5 (AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) covered by this item:** **Documentation and full suite** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (plugin root semantics, test-mode guard and store save behaviour) and any relevant wiki/docs entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and the existing seed/validation tests (`csv-seed.test.ts`, `configStore.*`, plugin tests, gym save tests) remain green.

- Documentation states, in the CSV/config area: (a) the plugin's write root is the
  Vite-resolved project root with an explicit override and requests escaping it are
  refused; (b) store saves are registry-only under vitest (`MODE === 'test'`) and
  read-write only in dev; (c) integration tests must install the CSV fetch bridge because
  relative fetches resolve against the happy-dom origin; (d) the suite asserts tracked CSVs
  are unchanged in both checkouts.
- Every claim in the docs matches the implemented behaviour (verified by reading the final
  code, not the plan).
- UK English prose, Markdown formatting, no duplicated statements of the same rule in
  multiple docs (link instead of copying).
- No new top-level planning document is added to the repo root.

## Key Files

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — CSV endpoint / config-store sections.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — headless/eval CSV read path if it mentions the dev endpoints.
- `README.md` — developer section mention of dev write-back/testing.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, `src/core/configStore.ts`, `src/test/setup.ts` —
  code comments (may already be written by the sibling items; this item verifies and
  consolidates).

## Minimal implementation (smallest end-to-end slice)

1. Read the final code from the sibling items and list the behaviours to document.
2. Update the smallest set of doc sections (links over duplication).
3. Verify each documented claim against the code (cite file + symbol in the commit
   message/comment).
4. Run `npm run build` (tsc/doc-adjacent checks) and the changed-scope suite via
   `/skill:test`.

## Notes / risks

- Sibling items own their own code comments (vertical slices); this item consolidates and
  fills gaps rather than duplicating prose.
- If a sibling item's implementation diverges from this plan's wording, the code wins —
  update the doc and note the divergence in a comment on this item.
data.title: Docs: CSV write-safety patterns and test isolation

## Goal

Drive the sortie-long warble from the shared pass so it starts at spawn and stops on every terminal, identically in the game and the gyms (parent AC1).

User story: As a player, I want to hear the classic UFO warble for the drone's whole sortie so I always know it is out there farming for me.

## Scope

- Start the warble exactly once at spawn in the shared spawn path (`spawnDrone`); stop it at every terminal: return-leg begin, payout/teardown, and destruction.
- Use the drone's phase-transition surface (`MysteryUfoDrone`) + `tickDrones` removal/teardown in `CombatCoreScene` so the same code runs in game and gyms (shared core only, gym-parity rule).
- Tests through the fixture recorder: start exactly once at spawn; stop called on return-leg begin, on payout, on destruction (incl. mid-sortie) and on teardown; no start/stop mismatch on repeated ticks; extend the cue contract with a stop-on-all-terminals assertion.

**Key Files:**
- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts`
- `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/audio/effects.ts`
- `src/test/collectorDroneFixtures.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Parent AC1 — warble lifecycle: a classic "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble cue plays continuously from spawn through the seek and collect phases (the whole sortie) and stops when the drone begins its return leg, pays out, is destroyed, or is torn down — delivered as a start/stop continuous cue with control companions (mirroring `stopDiveSound`/`stopThrusterSound`), at a level-appropriate audible gain that respects the shared SFX volume/mute settings.

scenario's bot-tuning **preset by name**, and seeds the run from the
scenario's seed — all through existing seams only, dev-gated exactly like

  the scenario's promo level.

# Fail fast on unwritable --out and invalid tune CSV

## Goal (user story)
As a developer running tune-loop verification I want `--tune` to validate `--out` (and the
balance CSV path) before anything expensive starts, so an invalid path fails in seconds with
an actionable message instead of running both sweeps first and then hanging or dying.

## Problem
`scripts/evaluate.mjs` only touches the output directory after both batches have run:
`executeTune()` calls `mkdirSync(options.outputDir, {recursive: true})` *after* the candidate
sweep (line ~394) and `main()` does the same for the non-tune path (line ~441). The 2026-10-21
negative probe (`--out /proc/nope/x`, 2 games x 200 ticks) therefore ran both sweeps and then
stalled for 166.6 minutes before an external SIGKILL (parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune --set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=7 --games 2 --ticks 200 --out <unwritable>`
  exits non-zero in well under two seconds, printing a single clear diagnostic on stderr.
- The probe runs **before** `loadCore()` (no Vite SSR boot) and before any `--tune` sweep.
- The `--tune` CSV target (`src/data/<tuneFile>`) is validated up-front too: a missing or
  unreadable CSV fails fast with its own message instead of failing after a baseline sweep.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Add an exported, unit-testable probe to `scripts/evaluate.mjs`, e.g.
   `ensureWritableOutputDir(dir)` → `{ok: true}` | `{ok: false, code, message}`:
   `mkdirSync(dir, {recursive: true})`, then write + `fsync` + unlink a sentinel file
   (`.evaluate-write-probe-<pid>`) so an unwritable-but-existing directory (`EACCES`) is
   caught, not just a non-creatable one (`ENOTDIR`, `EROFS`).
2. Export a matching `assertTuneInputs(csvPath)` (`readFileSync` probe) for the `--tune` CSV.
3. In `main()`, call the probes immediately after `parseEvaluateArgs`/`--help` handling and
   **before** `loadCore()`; on failure write `output directory not writable: <dir> (<code>)`
   (and the CSV equivalent) to stderr and return a non-zero exit code (2 — same class as the
   existing usage-error exit, documented in `EVALUATE_USAGE`).
4. Keep the late `mkdirSync` calls as a cheap idempotent safety net; do not duplicate the
   validity logic.
5. Update `EVALUATE_USAGE` and `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop → "Guards and guarantees")
   with the fail-fast validation, and extend the doc guard
   (`src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`) to assert the new statements.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The repro command fails fast (< 2 s) with a clear "output directory not writable" diagnostic and a non-zero exit, demonstrated after the fix (timings quoted in a work-item comment).
2. The writeability probe and CSV-path validation run before loadCore() and before any baseline or candidate sweep, proven by a test that observes no SSR boot on the failure path.
3. An unwritable-but-existing directory (EACCES) and a non-directory path (ENOTDIR) both fail fast, and the --tune CSV path is validated before the baseline sweep.
4. --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore and exits 0; existing behaviour is preserved and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.
5. CLI help (EVALUATE_USAGE) and docs/BALANCING.md mention the new validation, and the docs-guard test asserts it.
6. Unit tests cover the writeability probe and the CLI exit codes for each failure path, run under the project test policy (test skill).

Discovered-from: AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B
Depends-on: slice 1 (repro + red tests)

# Journal the tune CSV edit so a hard kill cannot leave it dirty

## Goal (user story)
As a developer I want the tune/edit cycle crash-safe, so that even an external SIGKILL, OOM or
timeout kill of the CLI never leaves `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` edited in the worktree — or,
if it does, the very next invocation (or a documented one-line command) restores it exactly.

## Problem
`executeTune()` applies the edit through `applyCsvEditFile()` and restores it in a `finally`
via `restoreCsvFile()` using the in-memory `attempt.originalText`. A SIGKILL runs no `finally`,
so the edited CSV survives the process (observed on 2026-10-21 immediately after the exit-137
kill, parent item AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B).

## Expected behaviour
- Before the first edited byte is written, a small journal (target path + original bytes) is
  persisted beside the CSV and fsynced.
- The journal is git-ignored, so a crashed run never shows up as a worktree change.
- After a successful restore (or with `--keep-edit`) the journal is removed.
- Any subsequent `scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` invocation that finds a stale journal first
  reconciles it (restores the original bytes, removes the journal, prints a warning) and then
  proceeds — so no manual step is needed in the normal case.
- A documented manual repair path exists for the case where the CSV must be restored without
  running the CLI again.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. New module `scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs`:
   `writeJournal(csvPath, originalBytes)` — write `<csvPath>.tune-journal` (JSON: csvPath,
   base64 original, pid, ISO timestamp) to a temp name, `fsync`, `rename` (atomic);
   `readJournal(path)`; `clearJournal(path)`; `reconcileJournal(path)` — restore original
   bytes when the journal exists, then delete it, returning `{action: 'restored'|'none'}`.
2. Wire into `executeTune()`: write the journal before `applyCsvEditFile`'s write, and clear
   it inside the existing `finally` after `restoreCsvFile()` resolves.
3. `main()` reconciles a stale journal for the `--tune` target before validation proceeds.
4. Add the journal pattern to `.gitignore` (e.g. `src/data/*.tune-journal`).
5. Document the guarantee + repair commands in `docs/BALANCING.md` (§Tuning loop →
   "Guards and guarantees"), and assert it in `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs
- scripts/evaluate-failfast.test.ts
- scripts/csvEdit-shell.test.ts
- src/utils/csvEdit.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A simulated hard kill (SIGKILL) after the edit leaves a journal; the next invocation restores the CSV byte-identical to the pre-run state, verified by a test that kills a child process and compares bytes.
2. The journal is written (fsynced, atomically renamed) beside the CSV before the edited bytes are written, and is removed after a successful restore or when --keep-edit is used.
3. The journal path is git-ignored so a crashed run leaves no worktree change, asserted by a .gitignore guard test.
4. A deterministic, documented repair path restores the CSV exactly, documented in docs/BALANCING.md together with the journal file name.
5. Unit tests cover the journal write, restore-from-journal and stale-journal reconciliation, run under the project test policy (test skill).
6. Existing tune behaviour is preserved: --tune with a valid --out still runs baseline -> edit -> re-run -> compare -> restore, exits 0, and existing evaluate/tune tests stay green.

# Per-run progress output and opt-in sweep watchdog

## Goal (user story)
As a developer (or an agent) running a long tune sweep I want visible per-run progress and an
opt-in bounded-runtime guard, so an abnormal run can never stall silently for hours and so a
timeout aborts cleanly with the CSV already restored.

## Problem
`--tune` prints nothing between start and the final summary: `executeTune()` runs two
`runBalanceBatch()` sweeps with no output. When the 2026-10-21 negative probe stalled, the only
signal was a silent process for 166.6 minutes until an external SIGKILL (parent item
AH-0MVIKLOOJ0058Z9B). After slice 2 the known hang is gone, but a future stall in the sweep
itself (configuration-driven blow-up, non-determinism guard loop, I/O stall) would again be
invisible.

## Expected behaviour
- Every `--tune` run writes one progress line per completed game to **stderr**:
  `[tune] baseline 1/2 seed=1 policy=competent`, then `[tune] candidate 2/2 …`, then the phase
  transitions (edit applied, comparing, restoring). Stdout stays byte-identical to today so
  artifact/print parity and determinism are preserved.
- `--watchdog <seconds>` (default `0` = off) arms a bounded-runtime guard: on expiry the run
  prints a diagnostic naming the phase and the elapsed time, restores the CSV (journal from
  slice 3 + synchronous restore), and exits with a distinct code (124) rather than leaving a
  killed-but-dirty worktree.
- `--help` and `docs/BALANCING.md` document both.

## Implementation sketch (smallest end-to-end slice)
1. Reuse the existing per-run hook instead of adding a second mechanism: `runBatch` already
   accepts `config.onRun` (`src/ai/eval/engine.ts`), but `runBalanceBatch()` in
   `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` does not expose it (and `CliOptions.telemetrySink` is ignored there).
   Add an optional second parameter `runBalanceBatch(options, hooks?: {onRun?})` that forwards
   `onRun`; keep the existing signature/behaviour when `hooks` is omitted.
2. In `executeTune()`, pass an `onRun` that writes the progress line to `io.err` (count games
   against `sweep.seeds.length * policies.length`) — no divergent copy of the sweep logic.
3. Add `--watchdog <seconds>` parsing to `parseEvaluateArgs` (validated: finite, >= 0;
   non-numeric → usage error exit 2), arm a timer in `executeTune()` and clear it in the
   existing `finally`; on expiry: diagnostic + `restoreCsvFile` + `process.exitCode = 124`
   (use `exitCode`, not `exit()`, so pending stderr drains and the pipe cannot mask the exit).
4. Docs: `docs/BALANCING.md` tune flags table + "Guards and guarantees"; assert in
   `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`.

## Risky assumptions
- A watchdog timer inside a synchronous sweep cannot interrupt a *blocking* synchronous call —
  it only fires between runs. Recorded as an accepted limitation: the guard catches stalls that
  yield to the event loop (the observed case is caught by slice 2's fail-fast path instead), and
  the progress lines remain the primary signal for a truly blocking stall. Document this
  limitation in `docs/BALANCING.md`.

## Key Files
- scripts/evaluate.mjs
- src/ai/eval/cli.ts
- src/ai/eval/engine.ts
- src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts
- scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts
- docs/BALANCING.md

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every --tune run emits per-run progress lines on stderr (never stdout), covered by a unit test that captures both streams.
2. An opt-in bounded-runtime watchdog (--watchdog <seconds>) aborts the sweep with a clear diagnostic naming the stalled phase, restores the CSV, and exits with a distinct non-zero code, covered by a test.
3. The full verification command used in AH-0MVBNLM2V008XC8T (including the negative probe) completes without hanging, with elapsed times recorded in a work-item comment.
4. Progress wiring reuses the shared runBatch onRun hook through runBalanceBatch (no divergent sweep copy in the shell), covered by cli.test.ts.
5. Artifact/print parity is preserved: stdout and the four tune artifacts are byte-identical to the pre-change output for the same seed/options (determinism tests stay green).
6. --help and docs/BALANCING.md document --watchdog, its default (off), its exit code, and the accepted limitation that a blocking synchronous stall cannot be interrupted, asserted by the docs guard.

# Relax single-type test pins to identity-preserving

## Summary / user story

**As a designer**, I want the campaign's documented level identities expressed as *dominance* assertions rather than *purity* assertions, so the producer's Q2=a decision ("preserve the dominant archetype, add variety around it") can be implemented without deleting the intent those pins protect.

The current suite pins Level 1 to "scouts only" and Level 5's filler waves to "phasers only". Those pins encode the very repetition the parent item removes. This feature replaces each purity pin with an equivalent, stricter-where-it-matters identity pin **before** the data changes land, so the tests document the intended end state.

## Scope

- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 "Level 1 uses Scout V-formations with no enemy fire".
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` AC1 Level 2 "mixed single-enemy waves" and Level 3 "mixed pairs" pins (keep the structural identity — one group per L2 wave, ≥2 archetypes per L3 wave — and relax only archetype purity).
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` phaser-only filler pins for Level 5.
- `src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts` — keep dominant-style, authoring-mix, showcase and difficulty pins exactly as they are; change only assertions that assume single-type purity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Level 1's pin asserts scout **dominance** (scouts present in every wave and the level's dominant archetype) plus its retained wave-1 Scout V-formation and the no-fire rule — not "scout is the only archetype".
2. Level 2's pin keeps the single-group-per-wave structure; Level 3's pin keeps ≥ 2 archetypes per wave; neither asserts archetype purity.
3. Level 5's pin asserts phaser dominance (phaser present in the majority of waves and dominant by spawned weight) instead of phaser-only composition.
4. Every relaxed assertion is accompanied by a UK-English code comment naming Q2=a on the parent item (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA) and explaining why purity was relaxed.
5. No assertion is deleted without a replacement of equal or stronger intent; `campaignInvariants.test.ts` showcase/mini-boss/ramp/fire-boundary assertions are unchanged.
6. Tests that were failing because of the future data change are re-expressed so they pass both before and after the data work (structural/identity assertions), or are explicitly marked pending with a recorded reason.


**Parent-AC traceability.** This item discharges the following acceptance criteria of the parent epic (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA), restated here so the link is explicit and auditable:
- **Parent AC3** — Each level keeps its dominant archetype identity (Level 1 Scout-dominant, Level 5 Phaser-dominant; classic-arcade levels keep their showcase archetypes), varying around it with secondary archetypes, verified by per-level dominant-archetype assertions and the GDD §3.2 identity text still holding.

## Minimal implementation

- Replace the `new Set(['scout'])` equality with a dominance + presence assertion helper.
- Reuse the dominant-archetype helper from `src/waves/campaignVariety.ts` (delivered by the audit feature) instead of duplicating weight logic in tests.
- Update the pin comments and record the rationale in this work item.

## Dependencies

- Requires the campaign-variety audit module (composition/dominance helpers, AC1–AC3 coverage).
- Must land **before** the Level 1/Level 5 pilot rework and the remaining levels' rework (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- Updated `WaveManager.test.ts`, `sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `campaignInvariants.test.ts` pins.
- Rationale comment on this work item.

**Key Files:**
- src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts
- src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts
- src/waves/campaignInvariants.test.ts
- src/waves/campaignVariety.ts

# Level 1 + Level 5 pilot: identity-preserving variety (vertical slice)

## Summary / user story

**As a player**, I want Level 1 and Level 5 to stop fielding one identical archetype for ten waves, while still feeling like "Entry" (scouts) and "Predictable Death" (phasers).

This is the **tracer-bullet** feature: the two hardest levels for the identity-vs-distinctness tension (the parent's highest risk) are reworked end-to-end — authored data, identity pins, campaign variety tests and code comments — before the remaining eight levels are touched. If the pattern works here, it is the template for the rest of the campaign.

## What to change

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` Level 1: scout-led waves with secondary archetypes introduced gradually (e.g. a diver or swarm escort appearing on alternating waves), keeping the gentle escalation, no enemy fire, and the wave-10 dense scout-phalanx mini-boss.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` Level 5: phaser-led waves with secondary archetypes varying around them (e.g. tank/diver escorts alternating), keeping the memorisable crosshair-grid feel and the wave-10 phaser+tank mini-boss.
- No new archetypes; existing roster only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Level 1: ten waves, ≥ 2 distinct archetypes across the level, **no adjacent pair sharing a composition**, scout dominant overall, `shootEnabled: false` on every wave, wave-10 `miniBoss: true` retained, wave 1 retains a Scout V-formation.
2. Level 5: ten waves, ≥ 2 distinct archetypes, **no adjacent pair sharing a composition**, phaser dominant overall, `shootEnabled: true`, wave-10 phaser+tank `miniBoss: true` retained.

4. If the campaign-wide aggregate assertion is still red because Levels 2–4 and 6–10 have not been reworked yet, it stays explicitly skip-marked with a reason pointing at the pending rework items — never silently deleted or weakened.
5. Identity pins from the pin-relaxation item pass unchanged for both levels.
6. Level comments in `Formations.ts` explain the secondary-archetype pattern in UK English, naming the parent item and the Q2=a decision.

# Enforce sequential distinctness for generated waves

## Summary / user story

**As a player**, I want generational (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves to also change their enemy mix wave-to-wave, so the guarantee cannot be broken just because a wave is produced by the sequencer rather than hand-authored.

Parent AC1 applies to **all** modes (producer Q3=c'). Today only twelve waves are generated, but the sequencer minimises difficulty error with no concept of the previous wave, so a generated wave can legally repeat its predecessor's archetype set.

## What to change

Add a **sequential-distinctness constraint** to the shared generated-wave path:

- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`: accept an optional "avoid these archetype sets" input (e.g. `SequencerOptions.avoidCompositions`) and, when the error-minimising composition matches an avoided set, deterministically select the next-best eligible candidate/composition instead.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`: track the previous wave's composition within a level and pass it in; `fixed` waves are never passed to the sequencer, so they remain exempt on the generated path (they are covered by authored data instead).
- `src/core/waveBalance.ts`: expose the composition signature / R4 distinctness rule as a named, documented rule beside R1–R3 so the sequencer and the campaign audit share one definition and one precedence order.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A generated wave never shares its archetype composition with the immediately preceding wave in the same level, across the shipped campaign at the default seed.
2. The constraint is deterministic: the same (curve, candidate pool, seed) always yields the identical campaign; no `Math.random`, no order-dependent iteration.
3. R1–R3 remain enforced and are audited over the rebuilt campaign; when distinctness and a balance rule conflict, **the balance rules win** and the resolution is documented next to the precedence.
4. Degenerate-input safety is preserved: an empty/one-entry candidate pool, or a level where no alternative composition exists, falls back to the best eligible composition rather than throwing or emitting an empty wave.
5. Target error is measured, not hidden: `campaignBalanceAudit` continues to report per-wave enforcement cost and the campaign stays inside the sequencer acceptance band; any wave that cannot satisfy distinctness within the band is recorded as follow-up authoring work rather than tolerated silently.
6. Unit tests cover: constraint satisfied; next-best fallback; no candidate left; `fixed` waves never constrained; `archetypeUsage` map not corrupted between waves.
7. No seeded-build regression: existing determinism and seed-divergence tests stay green.


**Parent-AC traceability.** This item discharges the following acceptance criteria of the parent epic (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA), restated here so the link is explicit and auditable:
- **Parent AC1** — No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition, verified by a unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config, applying to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.
- **Parent AC4** — Generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves continue to satisfy the classification balance rules R1–R3 (opening formation-only, no all-chaser wave, bounded ranged mix), verified by the existing `waveBalance` audit/validator tests passing over the rebuilt campaign.
- **Parent AC6** — The same seed reproduces the same campaign; `curve`/`fixed` waves stay seed-independent and `dynamic` waves remain a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed), verified by seeded-build equality tests as in the opening-variety item (AH-0MUOCJM0N000RW2B).

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `SequencerOptions` with an optional avoided-composition set; compute candidate compositions from the already-evaluated greedy result.
- Pass the previous wave's composition from `buildConfiguredLevel` in `sequencedLevels.ts`.
- Add the shared composition/rule helper to `src/core/waveBalance.ts` and reuse it in the audit module.
- Add the unit tests and extend the campaign audit with a distinctness check.

## Dependencies

- Campaign variety audit (shared composition signature).
- Can proceed in parallel with the Level 1/Level 5 pilot; **must** complete before the campaign-wide verification item.

## Deliverables

- Sequencer option + builder wiring + shared rule constant.
- Unit and campaign tests proving the constraint and its precedence.
- Target-error record in the audit output.

**Key Files:**
- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts
- src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts
- src/core/waveBalance.ts
- src/waves/campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts
- src/core/difficultySequencer.variety.test.ts

**As a player**, I want every level of the 100-wave campaign to change its enemy mix from wave to wave, so a run never feels like ten repetitions of the same encounter.

Levels 6–10 are handled by the sibling classic-arcade/finale item (same file, so the two land serially to avoid conflicting edits).

# Document and verify the fixed/curve/dynamic mode mix

## Summary / user story

**As a designer**, I want the per-wave generation mode ledger to be explicit and test-pinned, so it is clear which waves are hand-authored for identity/showcase and which are generated for per-run variety (producer Q3=c').

The parent adopts a **mixed** mechanism: authored `fixed` waves where a showcase/pin requires them, `curve` where determinism is wanted, and `dynamic` filler where seeded variety is safe. Today that mix is implicit in the CSV. This feature makes it a documented, verified contract, and converts a filler wave to `dynamic` **only** where the authored data cannot express the intent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented per-wave mode ledger (a table covering all 100 waves: level, wave, mode, and the one-line reason it holds that mode) is published in the GDD's default-campaign note.
2. A test asserts the shipped CSV/config **matches** the ledger: all three modes are used, every recorded showcase/opening/mini-boss wave is `fixed` (or its curated opening mode), and no unlisted wave silently changes mode.
3. For every `dynamic` wave the seeded-determinism contract holds (same seed ⇒ identical campaign; different seeds may differ) and AC1/R1–R3 still hold across a multi-seed sweep.
4. If a filler wave is converted to `dynamic`, the ledger records the conversion plus its reason and the wave remains within the sequencer acceptance band; if no conversion is warranted, the ledger records that decision explicitly as a documented no-op.
5. `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` header comments and `src/core/configStore.ts` comments describe the final mix and link the ledger.

# Campaign variety regression, determinism and full-suite verification

## Summary / user story

**As a maintainer**, I want one verification item that proves the rebuilt 100-wave campaign is varied, deterministic, balanced and regression-free, so the epic can be reviewed against its acceptance criteria with evidence rather than assertion.

## Scope

Verification only — no behaviour changes unless a genuine defect is found (which becomes a linked follow-up work item).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 evidence**: a campaign-wide assertion confirms zero adjacent composition duplicates across all 100 waves in the built campaign at the default config and seed, and a multi-seed sweep (≥ 3 seeds) keeps AC1 holding for generated waves.
2. **AC2/AС3 evidence**: the per-level archetype-count (≥ 2) and dominant-archetype identity assertions pass for all ten levels, and the recorded report is attached to this work item.
3. **AC4 evidence**: R1–R3 hold for every generated wave over the shipped campaign and across the seed sweep; the balance audit's per-wave enforcement cost stays inside the sequencer acceptance band.
4. **AC5 evidence**: the non-decreasing target ramp, the Levels 1–3 no-fire / Levels 4–10 fire boundary, the ten-wave-per-level shape, and the wave-10 mini-boss encounters are all still pinned and green, including the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins.
5. **AC6 evidence**: same-seed builds are byte-identical; `curve`/`fixed` waves are seed-independent; `dynamic` waves diverge across seeds. Determinism tests run over the rebuilt campaign.
6. **AC7 evidence**: the full project suite passes through the test skill; any failure is triaged into a critical `test-failure` work item with the blocking relationship recorded, and zero untriaged failures remain.
7. **Gym↔game parity evidence**: the campaign is built once in the shared core and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms — the parity assertions already in `src/waves/campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts` (AC3 gym↔game parity) and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stay green, and no divergent wave data copy is introduced.
8. The verification report (per-level archetype counts, adjacent-duplicate result, mode ledger snapshot, balance/target error summary) is recorded as a comment for audit.


**Parent-AC traceability.** This item discharges the following acceptance criteria of the parent epic (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA), restated here so the link is explicit and auditable:
- **Parent AC1** — No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition, verified by a unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config, applying to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.
- **Parent AC2** — All 100 waves are in scope (not just the opening four); every level's wave list shows more than one enemy archetype across its ten waves, verified by a per-level archetype-count assertion ≥ 2 across the ten waves.
- **Parent AC3** — Each level keeps its dominant archetype identity (Level 1 Scout-dominant, Level 5 Phaser-dominant; classic-arcade levels keep their showcase archetypes), varying around it with secondary archetypes, verified by per-level dominant-archetype assertions and the GDD §3.2 identity text still holding.
- **Parent AC4** — Generated (`curve`/`dynamic`) waves continue to satisfy the classification balance rules R1–R3 (opening formation-only, no all-chaser wave, bounded ranged mix), verified by the existing `waveBalance` audit/validator tests passing over the rebuilt campaign.
- **Parent AC5** — The non-decreasing target difficulty, the Levels 1–3 no-fire / Levels 4–10 fire boundary and the wave-10 mini-boss encounters are unchanged, and the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins pass, verified by the existing campaign regression and invariant suites.

- **Parent AC7** — New or updated unit/integration tests cover sequential distinctness, per-level identity, determinism and regression, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Minimal implementation

- Run the audit tooling over the built campaign; capture the report.
- Add/extend the seeded-build and determinism tests where coverage is missing.

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC2 "changes exactly on level change", AC3 warp timing/does-not-block, AC6 integration tests).

## Goal

As a player I want the new level's background to arrive with the warp exactly when the level changes (and never mid-level), so each of the ten levels is unmistakably a different place in space while gameplay, input and wave timing are untouched.

## Background

Level changes flow `WaveManager.onEnemyDestroyed()` → `'levelCleared'` → `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` → `_announceLevel()` + `_startTransition()` (`LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS = 1.5`). Two facts shape this slice:

1. **Two handlers.** The `levelCleared` case is duplicated in `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` and in `PlayScene._advanceAfterTimeout()` (the wave-timer expiry path). Both must reach the background swap, so the `levelCleared` work is extracted into one helper (e.g. `_onLevelCleared()`) that both call — otherwise a level cleared by timeout skips the swap.
2. **Level is already advanced.** `WaveManager` increments `_levelIndex` *before* returning `'levelCleared'`, so `waveManager.level` during the transition is the **incoming** level: the swap target is `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`, and the warp must finish no later than `transitionTimer` reaches 0 (`_onTransitionComplete()` then spawns the new wave).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On `'levelCleared'` only — not on `'waveCleared'`, not on `'bossTriggered'`, not per wave — `PlayScene` starts the warp and swaps to `backgroundForLevel(waveManager.level)`; the same code path is reached by both the kill path (`_handleWaveEvent`) and the wave-timeout path (`_advanceAfterTimeout`), with no duplicated background logic between them.
2. The warp is created at `_startTransition()` time for a level change, advanced from the scene's own tick (not wall-clock tweens), and is complete by the time the transition ends: after ticking `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` the background's `textureKey()` equals `backgroundForLevel(newLevel)`, `isComplete()` is true, and `_onTransitionComplete()` has spawned the wave on the unchanged frame schedule.
3. Non-blocking: during the warp the player still moves, auto-fires and can teleport, and the transition/wave timer schedule is unchanged — asserted by a test that ticks half the transition while driving input and checks bullets/position, plus an assertion that `transitionRemaining()` is unaffected by the warp's presence.
4. Boss entry keeps the final level's background (documented decision: no swap and no warp on `'bossTriggered'`); asserted by test so the boss arena's backdrop is deterministic.
5. Restart/shutdown safety: starting a new run or shutting the scene down mid-warp leaves no warp container, no stale background and no leaked timer — a subsequent level change behaves normally (tested).
6. New integration suite `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` covers ACs 1–5 and the existing `PlayScene` suites (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `PlaySceneHUD.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still pass unchanged; full-suite gate is left to the dev-push gate (no ad-hoc full runs).

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #6 — "Tests cover: deterministic level→background mapping, swap fires on level change (not wave), warp effect activates during the transition and completes within its duration, and the background layer does not intercept input; document updates (README, code comments, credits/attribution file with licences, GDD §3.2/§7.1 references as needed); the full project test suite passes with the new changes." — specifically the integration-tests half (swap-on-level-change-only, timing, input non-blocking, full suite); the documentation half is AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` first (boot via `src/test/gameHarness.ts`, drain a level to force `'levelCleared'`, use the fixture textures from the shared-layer slice).
- Extract `_onLevelCleared()` on `PlayScene`; both `_handleWaveEvent` and `_advanceAfterTimeout` call it (per the parent's "shared behaviour lives once" rule).
- In `_startTransition()`, take an optional `levelChanged` flag (or compare target level against the currently shown one) to start the warp; keep `_startTransition` otherwise identical so wave transitions are unaffected.
- Tick the warp from `update()` next to `transitionTimer`, and destroy it in `_onTransitionComplete()`/`teardownRunState()` (whichever owns cleanup) so completion and early shutdown are both safe.
- Keep the transition banner, wave timer and telemetry calls exactly as they are (no behaviour change beyond the backdrop/warp).

## Deliverables

- `PlayScene` level-change wiring: single `_onLevelCleared()` path, warp start, warp tick, cleanup.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` — integration suite (swap-on-level-change-only, timing, input non-blocking, boss behaviour, restart safety).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_handleWaveEvent`, `_advanceAfterTimeout`, `_startTransition`, `update`, `_onTransitionComplete`, `teardownRunState`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts` — new integration tests.
- `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.ts` — shared layer consumed by the wiring (no forking).
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` — warp module consumed by the wiring.
- `src/data/backgrounds.ts` — `backgroundForLevel` used for the swap target.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` / `src/scenes/SceneNavigation.test.ts` — regression coverage (read-only unless a fixture must be shared).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C (shared background layer); AH-0MVSEBCNC005G7XW (warp transition module); AH-0MVSEB2WZ000MZY8 (background assets, for real imagery in manual review).
- Blocks: AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV (documentation slice).

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC5: gym↔game parity, shared core, documented divergence).

## Goal

As a developer I want the gyms to consume the *same* background code as the shipped game — with any divergence explicit and justified — so the parity convention in AGENTS.md holds and gym-based visual review of the new backdrop is trustworthy.

## Background

`GymFormationScene` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) and the direct `CombatScene` gyms (`GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymWeaponLeveling`) all extend the shared core, so the lifecycle hooks from the shared-layer slice are inherited for free. What is *not* settled is whether a gym should show a backdrop at all: gyms compare enemies/weapons, and a photo backdrop could distract from the comparison, yet the AGENTS.md rule says an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in both places — so the decision has to be explicit and tested either way. `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (repo-wide duplicate-body guard) enforces "one implementation".

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Gyms render through the shared layer with **no** background code of their own: `GymFormationScene` and the `CombatScene`-based gyms either enable the shared `_createBackground()` (game-identical path) or skip it via one exported, documented switch — either way the duplicate-body guard passes with no new allow-list entries and no copied draw/swap logic.
2. One explicit, documented decision is recorded on the work item and in a code comment next to the switch, with the reason (e.g. "gyms pin the level-1 backdrop so enemy silhouettes are compared against a constant backdrop, no level-change warp because gyms do not change campaign levels").
3. If gyms enable backgrounds: the gym's backdrop is a fixed representative level (`backgroundForLevel(1)`), no warp is ever triggered, and it still renders at depth ≤ −1000, non-interactive, with the same dim overlay as the game — asserted by test.
4. `src/scenes/gym/backgroundParity.test.ts` boots one formation gym and `PlayScene` with the shared fixture textures and asserts: same layer module/helper is used, identical depth/dim/non-interactive invariants, and the documented divergence (fixed level, no warp) — so a future change to one without the other fails a test.
5. All existing gym suites (`src/scenes/gym/*.test.ts`, including `GymIndex.test.ts`) pass unchanged; changed-scope gate passes.
6. Where the divergence is non-obvious, a note is added to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 parity convention (a one-line link is enough; the docs slice owns the fuller write-up).

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #5 — "Background creation/swap logic lives in the shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/`) consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms (gym↔game parity convention in AGENTS.md); any gym divergence is documented." — specifically the gym adoption + documented-divergence half; the shared-core home is AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the parity test first (it can start as a red assertion that the gym's backdrop matches the game's invariants).
- Add the opt-in/opt-out switch at the shared base (`GymFormationScene`), not per gym — one decision, inherited by every formation gym; direct `CombatScene` gyms pick it up through the same base hooks.
- Reuse `src/test/backgroundFixtures.ts` from the shared-layer slice rather than adding gym-specific texture stubs.
- Record the decision in the completion comment and in the parent's Appendix so it is auditable; do not silently diverge.

## Deliverables

- Gym adoption switch (or documented opt-out) in the shared gym base, inherited by all gyms.
- `src/scenes/gym/backgroundParity.test.ts` — gym↔game background parity tests.
- One-line parity note where divergence is non-obvious.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — shared gym base; single adoption switch.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` / `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` / `GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` / `GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — direct `CombatScene` gyms (verify, edit only if they need the switch).
- `src/scenes/gym/backgroundParity.test.ts` — new parity tests.
- `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.ts` — shared layer (must not be forked).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body guard (read-only unless the guard must list the new shared surface).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §5.1 parity note.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C (shared background layer).
- Blocks: none — AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV (docs) references the recorded decision.

# Authored variety rework — Levels 6–10 (classic-arcade + finale)

## Summary / user story

**As a player**, I want the classic-arcade showcase levels and the finale to change their enemy mix wave to wave instead of replaying the same authored compositions, so the back half of the campaign stays varied.

Second half of the bulk data work (Levels 1–5 are covered by the pilot and the onboarding rework items): re-mix the hand-authored `fixed` waves of Levels 6–10 so **no two sequential waves share an archetype composition**, while every classic-arcade debut and the final gauntlet keep their identity.

## Scope

- `src/waves/Formations.ts` static `LEVELS` data for Levels 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.
- Keep every showcase wave `fixed` with its debuting archetype and spawner opt-in: L6 `march`/`capturer`, L7 `centipede`/`ghosts`, L8 `laneTraffic`/`horde`/`raider`, L9 phaser siege + `ghosts` (the `orbital-strike` hazard stays a non-blocking hazard, never a wave group), L10 raider+capturer finale.
- Keep the existing `curve` rows for these levels working; do **not** invent archetypes or rework mini-boss encounters.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. For Levels 6–10, **no adjacent wave pair shares an archetype composition**, verified through the shared audit module, and those level-scoped AC1 assertions are activated and green when this item lands (AC1 for this slice). This item is the one that activates the **campaign-wide** AC1/AC2 aggregate assertion, which must be fully green when it lands.
2. Levels 6–10 each show **≥ 2 distinct archetypes** across their ten waves (AC2).
3. Per-level dominance matches `LEVEL_IDENTITY` (AC3): L6 march-dominant, L7 segmented/pursuit showcase, L8 lane/horde/raider showcase, L9 phaser siege, L10 gauntlet mix.
4. Every showcase wave, spawner opt-in flag and wave-10 `miniBoss` survives unchanged in kind; `campaignInvariants.test.ts` showcase coverage, player-targeter pairing and classic-arcade-debut pins stay green.
5. Spawner opt-in density stays bounded as documented (the `ghosts`/`horde`/`laneTraffic` flags are not sprayed across every filler wave) so wave accounting and performance stay as designed.
6. `orbital-strike` is never added as a wave group (it is a non-wave-accounted hazard; adding it would soft-lock wave clearance).
7. The `targetDifficulty` rows stay non-decreasing and the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K pins pass (AC5); Levels 6–10 remain firing levels.
8. Per-level comments in `Formations.ts` describe each level's dominant archetype and its secondary mix, in UK English.


**Parent-AC traceability.** This item discharges the following acceptance criteria of the parent epic (AH-0MVI5XXOU00954EA), restated here so the link is explicit and auditable:
- **Parent AC1** — No two sequential waves anywhere in the built campaign (Levels 1–10 × 10 waves, `buildSequencedLevels()` output) share the same enemy composition, verified by a unit/integration test asserting pairwise distinctness of adjacent waves across all 100 waves at default config, applying to `curve`, `dynamic` and `fixed` modes alike.
- **Parent AC2** — All 100 waves are in scope (not just the opening four); every level's wave list shows more than one enemy archetype across its ten waves, verified by a per-level archetype-count assertion ≥ 2 across the ten waves.
- **Parent AC3** — Each level keeps its dominant archetype identity (Level 1 Scout-dominant, Level 5 Phaser-dominant; classic-arcade levels keep their showcase archetypes), varying around it with secondary archetypes, verified by per-level dominant-archetype assertions and the GDD §3.2 identity text still holding.
- **Parent AC5** — The non-decreasing target difficulty, the Levels 1–3 no-fire / Levels 4–10 fire boundary and the wave-10 mini-boss encounters are unchanged, and the AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K regression pins pass, verified by the existing campaign regression and invariant suites.

## Minimal implementation

- Work level by level using the same pattern proven in the pilot and onboarding items: keep the identity anchor group, rotate 1–2 secondary archetypes across waves, prefer changing the archetype *set* over counts.
- Run the audit module's per-level report after each level; record the result in a comment.
- Preserve the `group()`/`openFire()` helper style and formation kinds.

## Dependencies

## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
paired implementation item for "Test the wheel slot distribution and outcome
resolver": this item makes those tests green.

## Summary

New Phaser-free pure module `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` owning the wheel's
mathematics and the single reward-application entry point, so `PlayScene` and
any gym consume identical code (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1). The
scene never computes probabilities — it receives the resolved outcome.

## Design

- `MINI_BOSS_WHEEL_SLOT_COUNT = 100`; the distribution is a single named
  constant: 1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single.
- `buildWheelWedges(ownedKinds)` → one wedge per owned permanent kind plus one
  bonus wedge, in a stable order (weapons first, then power-ups, matching
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`).
- `drawWheelOutcome(slotIndex, ownedKinds)` → a resolved outcome
  `{ gains: Array<{ id, levels }> }` for a slot index 0–99 drawn by the
  caller's injected run-seeded RNG (single/double/triple/bonus). A
  multi-upgrade slot selects **distinct** owned kinds where possible, repeating
  a kind only when there are fewer owned kinds than the slot's count.
- `applyWheelOutcome(outcome, effectsRegistry, player)` → applies every gain
  exactly once through the shared `applyMineralChoiceReward` seam (one
  `weapon-level`/`power-up-level` choice-option per level-gain step), so the
  awarded levels run the identical permanent-level machinery as the hold-full
  choice.
- **No level-cap filtering** — parity with `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`, which
  offers level-ups with no cap check; every level always counts (see parent
  OPEN QUESTION 1).
- Module-level JSDoc documents the distribution, the distinct-pick rule and
  the "a mini-boss always pays out" invariant (parent AC3/AC4).

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (new)
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` (consumed unchanged — shared reward seam)
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` (`buildLevelUpOption` / `toChoiceOption` consumed)
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` (`resolveSlotState().ownedIds` feeds the wedge list)
- `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` (paired test item)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Test the wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver"
- Blocks: "Launcher-agnostic mini-boss wheel overlay scene", "Rework PlayScene
  mini-boss reward to the wheel"
- Related: parent AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD (AC3, AC6)

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` is a pure, Phaser-free **shared module** exporting the **100-slot distribution** (1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single) from a single named constant, and a weighted outcome resolver over the owned permanent kinds.
- Outcomes are drawn from the **run-seeded RNG** (injectable, no `Math.random()`, no wall clock) so the same seed and owned-kind snapshot reproduce the same outcome.
- Multi-upgrade slots pick **distinct** owned kinds where possible and repeat a kind only when there are fewer owned kinds than the slot's count (one owned kind landing a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
- The bonus outcome resolves to +1 level on every owned permanent kind.
- A single shared application entry point applies a resolved outcome exactly once through `applyMineralChoiceReward`, so the distribution/resolver and the reward application live in shared modules the game and gyms both consume.
- The wedge list and the weighted outcome are derived from the same owned-kind snapshot (`resolveSlotState().ownedIds`); the module never requires a scene or a Phaser type and never computes probabilities for display.
- The paired test item's tests pass and the changed-scope gate is green.

## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
paired implementation item for "Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin
behaviour": this item makes those tests green.

## Summary

New launcher-agnostic wheel overlay scene `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`
mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s overlay pattern (pause, single optional
result callback, demo auto-select contract). The scene receives the owned-kind
wedges and a resolved outcome from the launcher; it only animates and reports,
never computes probabilities.

## Design

- Registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts` so `scene.launch('MiniBossWheelScene',
  …)` works everywhere.
- Payload: `wedges` (one per owned permanent kind + bonus wedge, each carrying
  the code-drawn icon + display name), `outcome` (target wedge index + extra
  gained wedges for multi-upgrade spins), optional `onResult` callback
  (mirrors `MineralChoiceScene.onSelect`), and optional `autoSpinMs`
  (demo mode: after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`) / `fireSchedule` (reduced-
  volume ghost fire while paused, reusing the shared hold-full metronome).
- Spin: pointer click or any keyboard key starts a fast-start, ease-out
  rotation (≈2.2 s total, at most one overshoot revolution, duration exported
  as a constant) that stops on the target wedge; the landed wedge is
  highlighted; the result callback fires exactly once; a later spin is a
  no-op.
- **Multi-upgrade reveal (producer answer Q2):** when the outcome grants 2–3
  kinds, the landing wedge renders **all** the gained kinds' icons inside that
  one wedge ("all icons present") — the other gained kinds are not lit up on
  separate wedges — so the complete result is legible at the pointer.
- Tension over predictability: the wedge list order and the target angle are
  hidden from the player until the spin stops (outcome resolved by the
  launcher from the run-seeded RNG before launch).
- Code-first visuals only (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new)
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` (register the scene)
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` (reused unchanged)
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (pattern reference)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution, consumed unchanged)
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MiniBossWheelScene.test.ts` (paired test item)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin behaviour" and "Pure
  wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver"
- Blocks: "Rework PlayScene mini-boss reward to the wheel", "Prove gym↔game
  parity for the mini-boss wheel reward"
- Related: parent AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD (AC1, AC2, AC6)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A wheel overlay scene exists (`src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`), registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`, presenting **one wedge per owned permanent kind** across the shared six-slot pool (power-up kinds **and** weapon drops) **plus a single bonus wedge**, drawn with the existing code-drawn icons; the upgrade-or-unlock menu is never shown through this surface.
- Play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice while the overlay is open, and the overlay closes and gameplay resumes when the result callback completes.
- Spinning is **player-initiated** (click/keyboard): the wheel animation starts fast and eases out (≈2.2 s total, at most one overshoot revolution, duration exported as a constant), the outcome is not predictable until it stops, and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly once.
- A **multi-upgrade outcome's landing wedge shows all the gained kinds' icons** in that one wedge (producer answer Q2 — "the wedge with the multi-results has all icons present"), with no separate highlights on other wedges, and the whole outcome applied exactly once.
- Level-saturated kinds are **not** filtered out of the draws (producer answer Q1 = Option A): the wheel matches the hold-full choice and a spin always increments levels.
- The scene is launcher-agnostic: it receives the wedges and the resolved outcome, exposes a **single optional result callback** (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene.onSelect`), never computes probabilities itself, and never reaches into a launcher by key.
- Demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls; normal play waits for input.
- The paired test item's tests pass and the changed-scope gate is green.

## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
paired implementation item for "Test the PlayScene wheel reward flow and
empty-owned fallback": this item makes those tests green.

## Summary

Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` / `selectMiniBossReward` so a mini-boss
defeat launches the wheel overlay with the owned permanent kinds, applies the
resolved outcome exactly once through the shared reward machinery, falls back
to the hold-full-style three-option choice when nothing permanent is owned,
and keeps the demo auto-spin. The unlock machinery is already removed (parent
AC5, sibling item).

## Design

- Open: build the owned-kind snapshot once from
  `resolvePlayerSlotState(this.player).ownedIds`
  (power-up kinds and weapon drops; permanent view). When empty →
  **fallback**: open the shared `MineralChoiceScene` with the hold-full-style
  three options (`createRandomChoiceStrategy` / `chooseOptions`), applied
  permanently — a mini-boss always pays out (AC4).
- When populated: resolve the wheel outcome once from the run-seeded RNG
  (`drawWheelOutcome`/`miniBossWheel`) and launch `MiniBossWheelScene` with the
  wedges, the outcome and a single result callback. Pause exactly like the
  hold-full choice; pass the frozen fire schedule for the reduced-volume ghost
  fire; rebase the beat clock on resume.
- Select/result: apply the outcome once via `applyWheelOutcome`
  (shared reward seam), close the overlay, resume play, reset the open flag —
  a repeated select is a no-op.
- Demo mode: pass `autoSpinMs: BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot
  auto-spins from the run-seeded RNG and never stalls.
- Test getters (`getMiniBossRewardOptions`, `isMiniBossRewardOpen`) preserved
  or re-homed so the wheel-flow tests keep a stable surface.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (rework `openMiniBossReward` /
  `selectMiniBossReward`; drop unlock state)
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (launched overlay)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution + application)
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` (`resolvePlayerSlotState` — owned kinds)
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` (`chooseOptions` for the fallback)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`
  (paired test item)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Test the PlayScene wheel reward flow and empty-owned fallback",
  "Launcher-agnostic mini-boss wheel overlay scene", "Pure wheel slot
  distribution and outcome resolver" and "Remove the weapon-unlock reward
  feature and bump checkpoint version"
- Blocks: "Prove gym↔game parity for the mini-boss wheel reward",
  "Document the wheel reward and unlock removal"
- Related: parent AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC6)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Defeating a mini-boss opens the **wheel overlay** with one wedge per owned permanent kind across the shared six-slot pool (power-up kinds and weapon drops) plus a single bonus wedge; the multi-option upgrade-or-unlock choice is gone and play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice.
- The spin is player-initiated, and the resolved outcome (from the 100-slot distribution via the shared resolver) is applied **exactly once** through the shared reward machinery — a repeated select/spin is a no-op.
- **Empty-owned fallback:** when the player owns no permanent kinds at a mini-boss defeat, the wheel is not shown and the existing hold-full-style three-option choice is offered instead, so a mini-boss always pays out.
- Demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` from the run-seeded RNG so the attract bot never stalls.
- No `Math.random()` or unlock-state remains in the reward path; the wheel flow consumes the shared modules only.
