# Intake brief — Timed consumable field pickups should use the absorbed-hit model (AH-0MVUVSW4J0009QUW)

**Type:** feature · **Priority:** medium · **Discovered from:** AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW ·
**Blocked by:** AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (dependency edge, parent plan `plan_complete`)

**Producer decisions (2026-10-30):** Q-A1 = **b** (a pickup's charge does **not**
regenerate — one drop buys one event, then the item is inert) · Q-A2 = **a**
(temporary-level TTL reuses today's windows: Shield 15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force
Field 8 s) · Q-A3 = **resolved** (AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P is not delivered
separately). See [Decisions](#decisions-producer-2026-10-30).

## Headline

A **field pickup** of Shield, Thorn Field or Force Field should buy **one charge
of one event** (one absorbed hit / one free ram / one reflected bullet) from the
shared consumable charge pool that AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW introduces, instead of
opening a level-resolved **timed window** — and that pickup charge is **not
backed by regeneration**, so a single drop is worth exactly one event. The three
per-kind window axes retire and their level curves re-point at the charge cap /
regeneration interval, so a pickup and a hold-full grant share one model, one
HUD row and one code path, differing only in whether the pool refills.

## Original seed (as filed)

Convert the **timed field pickups** of the budget/consumable power-ups (Shield,
Thorn Field, Force Field) to the same one-event charge model the permanent
consumable pool uses, so a pickup spends a single event (one absorbed hit / one
free ram / one reflected bullet) instead of opening a timed window.

Produced by the producer's answer to **Q2** on AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (*Consumable
upgrades should not be endless*): one charge buys one single event (option b),
and the timed-pickup conversion is deliberately split into this follow-up so that
change lands after the permanent-charge model.

## Problem statement

The run-scoped model now has **two contradictory shapes for the same item**. A
hold-full grant of Shield/Thorn Field/Force Field becomes a **charge pool** (one
event per charge, level-derived cap and regeneration, HUD countdown —
AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW), while a **field pickup** of the same item still opens a
**level-resolved timed window** with its own parallel budget counter and its own
HUD countdown. The player sees "one absorbed hit" from one acquisition path and
"up to 18 seconds of cover" from the other, and the effect path keeps two
mechanisms (window + budget) for what the design calls one thing.

## Users

- **The player** who collects Shield / Thorn Field / Force Field from a drop and
  wants the same legible "one hit, then it comes back" behaviour they get from a
  hold-full grant — not a timer that means a different thing per acquisition
  path.
- **The balance owner**, who needs one bounded unit of value ("one absorbed
  hit") with one level axis pair (cap + regeneration) instead of a window
  duration that silently changes how many events the same pickup buys.
- **The maintainer**, who wants the window machinery deleted rather than
  parallel-cased for three kinds.

**User stories**

- "As a player, when I collect a Shield drop I get **one** absorbed hit — not a
  15-second bubble — and the HUD row tells me when the next absorption is due."
- "As a player, when I collect Thorn Field I get **one** free ram, and when I
  collect Force Field I get **one** reflected bullet; each of them recharges on
  the same rhythm the hold-full version uses."
- "As a balance owner, the three kinds have exactly two level axes each — a
  charge cap and a regeneration interval — and no window duration that changes
  the number of events a pickup is worth."

## Existing state (verified in the repo)

The timed windows for the three kinds are one mechanism with three
instantiations:

- **Shield** — `_applyTimedEffect` opens `shieldDuration` (base 15 s → cap 30 s)
  and sets `_shieldRemaining` to `shieldAbsorptions` (base 1 → cap 3)
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:531-543`); `tryAbsorbShield()` decrements the
  registry-local counter and the last absorption pops the bubble
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:828`).
- **Thorn Field** — `thornsDuration` (8 s → 16 s) window plus `_thornsRemaining`
  from `thornsAbsorbs` (2 → 6), with an **intra-window** refill on
  `thornsRecharge` (12 s → 5 s) that is explicitly gated on the window being
  open (`_advanceThornsRecharge` early-returns via `!this._timed.has('thorns')`,
  `src/powerups/effects.ts:1196-1202`);
  `thornsRechargeRemaining()` returns 0 when there is no active window
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:1177`).
- **Force Field** — `forceFieldDuration` (8 s → 18 s) bubble plus
  `_forceFieldRemaining` from `forceFieldReflects` (3 → 10)
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:588-604`); `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` at
  `src/powerups/effects.ts:922`; the spent-but-dim visual persists after the
  budget is gone (AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z).
- **Catalogue** — the three window axes exist as first-class level variables
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` at `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:219/238/249`;
  specs at `:311`, `:755`, `:892`; stat fields at `:1061`, `:1108`, `:1133`).
- **HUD** — the only consumable regeneration countdown today is Thorn Field's,
  `_powerUpRecharge()` case `'thorns'` → `thornsRechargeRemaining()`
  (`src/ui/HUD.ts:574-580`); Shield and Force Field show no countdown at all.
- **Field-pickup levelling** — a pickup adds one **temporary** level stack and
  the temporary component is cleared by `clearTemporary(id)` when the window
  expires (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:1466-1474`); kinds with no timed
  window keep their temporary stack for the run (Resolved decision 4,
  documented at `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:63-66`). A temporary stack
  occupies a six-slot slot for as long as it lasts
  (`getTempPowerUpIds()`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:1459`).
- **Checkpoints** — permanent grants are replayed through the shared grant seam
  on resume; temporary field-pickup windows are deliberately not persisted and
  never re-open (`docs/Game Design Document.md:1769`).
- **Docs** — the three kinds are documented as *timed* in the GDD player-facing
  table (`docs/Game Design Document.md:965` Shield, `:974` Force Field) and in
  the per-kind level-axis table at `:1196`/`:1205`/`:1209`, with behaviour notes
  at `:1189` (Force Field axes) and `:1190` (Thorn visibility + recharge) and
  the acquisition model at `:1180`.

## Desired change

1. A **field pickup** (`applyCollect(id, false)`) of `shield`, `thorns` or
   `force_field` grants **exactly one charge** into the shared consumable charge
   pool AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW introduces (clamped at the level-resolved cap) and
   **opens no effect window**. The pickup still adds its existing **one
   temporary level stack** (field-pickup levelling is unchanged — the temporary
   stack raises the cap/interval while it lasts and reverts on its own TTL,
   which the sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A supplies); charges already granted
   are **never clawed back** when that TTL expires (AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC
   resolved decision 2).
2. **A pickup-granted charge does not regenerate (producer decision Q-A1=b).**
   A single drop buys **exactly one event** and the item is **inert afterwards**:
   no charge is banked back for a consumable the player only ever picked up.
   Regeneration is gated on **permanent ownership** — the pool's regenerating
   ceiling for these three kinds is `permanentGrants(id) > 0 ? cap : 0`, so an
   item that was never a hold-full grant never refills on its own. The gate is
   **catalogue data** (a consumable property alongside the parent's `consumable`
   flag), not a per-kind `id === …` special case, and it is **scoped to these
   three kinds**: the shipped regenerating behaviour of Phase Shift / Teleport
   field pickups (AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT) is unchanged.
3. **One charge = one event**, spent through the existing shared consumption
   seams with no new counter: `tryAbsorbShield()` spends one charge (one
   absorbed hit), `tryConsumeThornsRam()` spends one charge (one free ram),
   `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect()` spends one charge (one reflected bullet).
   The registry-local `_shieldRemaining` / `_thornsRemaining` /
   `_forceFieldRemaining` counters are replaced by pool-derived accessors, so
   there is one source of truth per kind.
4. **Armed means "holds a charge"** — the bubble/aura is drawn while the pool
   has at least one charge and pops when the last charge is spent (the existing
   pop-on-last-absorb path), so the final-second wind-down animation of the
   timed window has no trigger left for Shield and must be either re-pointed at
   the TTL or documented as retired (dead-code decision recorded, not silently
   dropped).
5. **The three window axes retire.** `shieldDuration`, `thornsDuration` and
   `forceFieldDuration` are removed from `PowerUpLevelVariable`,
   `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` and
   `PowerUpLevelStats`; no replacement window axis is introduced. The three
   kinds keep exactly two axes each — the parent's charge cap and regeneration
   interval (`shieldAbsorptions` + new `shieldRecharge`; `thornsAbsorbs` +
   `thornsRecharge`; `forceFieldReflects` + new `forceFieldRecharge`).
6. **The per-kind window TTL resolver must be updated with the retirement.** The
   sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A resolves a temporary-window TTL per kind
   (timed kinds → their level-resolved effect duration, instant kinds → a
   declared `temporaryWindow` value). After this change these three kinds are
   **instant kinds** for that resolver, so they declare flat `temporaryWindow`
   values (producer decision Q-A2=a) and must not be read through
   `stats.shieldDuration` / `stats.thornsDuration` /
   `stats.forceFieldDuration`.
7. **HUD** — after a pickup these three kinds show the charge count on the
   shared consumable row and **no window countdown**; because a pickup-only
   charge never regenerates, the row shows **no regeneration countdown** either
   (there is nothing to count down), is greyed while owned-and-empty, and
   disappears once the temporary-level TTL expires (the existing field-only
   rule). A **permanently granted** item keeps the parent's full behaviour (live
   `next in Ns` countdown, greyed empty row). The parent's HUD work
   (AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6) owns the rendering; this item owns the assertion that a
   **pickup** lands in the right row state, and removes the Thorn-specific
   `_powerUpRecharge` special case in favour of the shared consumable path.
8. **Parity** — every change lands in the shared core
   (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`,
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) so `PlayScene` and every gym that spawns or
   consumes these kinds inherit it; the duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` assertions stay green, and the parity matrix rows for
   these kinds are updated where the retained divergences change.

### Per-kind conversion table

| Kind | Today (field pickup) | After (field pickup) |
|---|---|---|
| Shield | 15 s → 30 s bubble + 1 → 3 absorptions, refreshed on re-collect | 1 charge = **1 absorbed hit**, held until used; **no regeneration** from a pickup; cap `shieldAbsorptions` (1 → 3) and regeneration `shieldRecharge` (45 s → shorter) only once the item is permanently owned; temporary level TTL **15 s** |
| Thorn Field | 8 s → 16 s window + 2 → 6 rams, refilled every 12 s → 5 s *while the window is open* | 1 charge = **1 free ram**, held until used; **no regeneration** from a pickup; cap `thornsAbsorbs` (2 → 6) and regeneration `thornsRecharge` (12 s → 5 s) only once permanently owned; temporary level TTL **8 s** |
| Force Field | 8 s → 18 s bubble + 3 → 10 reflects | 1 charge = **1 reflected bullet**, held until used; **no regeneration** from a pickup; cap `forceFieldReflects` (3 → 10) and regeneration `forceFieldRecharge` (45 s → shorter) only once permanently owned; temporary level TTL **8 s** |

So a drop is worth exactly **one event** (the producer's Q-A1=b scarcity rule), while a
hold-full grant keeps the parent's regenerating pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — A pickup grants exactly one charge and no effect window.** A Shield /
  Thorn Field / Force Field field pickup adds exactly one charge to the shared
  consumable pool, clamped at the level-resolved cap, and opens no effect
  window: no `shieldDuration` / `thornsDuration` / `forceFieldDuration` read
  remains on the path, and the registry's timed map never holds these ids after
  a pickup. It still adds its one temporary level stack. Tests assert pool count
  and clamp per kind, the absence of a window, and that the temporary-stack TTL
  expiry leaves the granted charge intact (no clawback).
- **AC2 — One charge resolves exactly one event and a pickup charge never
  regenerates.** Each spent charge resolves exactly one event (Shield one
  absorbed hit, Thorn Field one free ram, Force Field one reflected bullet); a
  **pickup-only** item then stays empty and **inert** — no regeneration clock
  starts, and a long tick grants nothing (`permanentGrants(id) === 0` ⇒
  regenerating ceiling 0). A **permanently granted** item keeps the parent's
  spend→empty→regenerate→re-use cycle. Both cycles are asserted per kind, in
  `PlayScene`'s shared core and in a gym, with no duplicate counter left behind
  (`_shieldRemaining` / `_thornsRemaining` / `_forceFieldRemaining` removed or
  derived); a regression test pins that Phase Shift / Teleport pickup
  regeneration is unchanged.
- **AC3 — HUD shows the pickup charge with no countdown that cannot happen.**
  After a field pickup the kind's HUD row shows the charge count and **no**
  regeneration or window countdown (a pickup-only charge never regenerates), the
  row is greyed while empty and disappears when the temporary-level TTL expires;
  a permanently granted item's row keeps the parent's live `next in Ns`
  countdown and greyed-empty state. HUD tests cover each state per kind and
  assert that a pickup row never renders a countdown it cannot honour, and the
  Thorn-specific `_powerUpRecharge` case is replaced by the shared consumable
  path.
- **AC4 — The window axes are retired, not orphaned.** `shieldDuration`,
  `thornsDuration` and `forceFieldDuration` are absent from
  `PowerUpLevelVariable`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`, `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` and
  `PowerUpLevelStats`, with no remaining reference in `src/` outside tests that
  assert their removal; the change-summary/deferred-axis seam
  (`DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`) stays consistent, and the per-kind
  temporary-window TTL resolver classifies the three kinds as instant kinds with
  the producer-approved flat values — **Shield 15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force
  Field 8 s** (coordinated with AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A).
- **AC4b — The no-regeneration gate is catalogue data, not a special case.**
  The "a pickup charge does not regenerate until the item is permanently owned"
  rule is expressed as a consumable property in `src/powerups/types.ts` and read
  by the store/registry; no `id === 'shield' | 'thorns' | 'force_field'` branch
  appears outside the catalogue, and the gate is scoped so Phase Shift / Teleport
  pickup regeneration is unchanged (regression-tested).
- **AC5 — Game and gym behave identically.** All behaviour runs through the
  shared store/registry/`CombatScene` seams; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`
  and the `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` docs assertions pass, and the parity matrix rows
  for the three kinds are updated where a retained divergence changes.
- **AC6 — Checkpoint resume is unchanged and singled out.** A pickup-earned
  charge is not persisted and no window re-opens on resume (existing rule,
  `docs/Game Design Document.md:1769`); a permanent grant still replays through
  the shared grant seam into the same charged state. Regression test asserts
  both, so the conversion cannot quietly start persisting temporary state.
- **AC7 — Documentation updated.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4
  (the player-facing rows at `:965` / `:974`, the acquisition model at `:1180`,
  the behaviour notes at `:1189` / `:1190`, and the per-kind level-axis table at
  `:1196` / `:1205` / `:1209`) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` describe the
  absorbed-hit pickup model, the two axes per kind and the HUD countdown; the
  `src/powerups/effects.ts` and `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` module headers
  no longer describe these kinds as timed.
- **AC8 — Tests and full suite.** New/updated unit tests cover the store grant
  path, the three consumption seams, the retired axes and the HUD row states;
  the full project test suite passes with the change (run through the test
  skill; the dev-push gate enforces it).

## Constraints

- **Must land after AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW.** The shared charge pool, the
  charge/regeneration accessors and the HUD row work are that item's; this item
  consumes them and must not implement a parallel pool.
- **No parallel implementation.** One pool, one grant path, one spend path per
  kind — the shared store/registry seams, never a per-scene copy.
- **No rebalance beyond the model.** Do not change the shipped caps
  (`shieldAbsorptions` 1 → 3, `thornsAbsorbs` 2 → 6, `forceFieldReflects`
  3 → 10) or the parent's regeneration curves; the only value changes are the
  retired window axes and the producer-approved temporary-level TTLs (Shield
  15 s, Thorn Field 8 s, Force Field 8 s).
- **Scarcity rule (Q-A1=b).** A pickup-granted charge is worth **one event** and
  never refills unless the item is permanently owned; do not soften this into a
  token regeneration "just for pickups", and do not extend the rule to Phase
  Shift / Teleport, whose shipped pickup regeneration (AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT) is
  unchanged.
- **No clawback.** Charges already granted survive a temporary-level TTL
  expiry (AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC resolved decision 2).
- **Coordinate with in-flight work on the same surface:**
  - AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P (*Permanent Force Field should regenerate its reflect
    budget*, blocked/intake_complete) — **producer decision Q-A3: resolved, do
    not deliver it separately.** Its remaining scope (a `forceFieldRecharge`
    axis + dim-to-bright refill + countdown) is **subsumed** by the parent for
    permanents and by this item for pickups, so it has been **re-scoped** (not
    deleted, so the requirement cannot be lost if the parent changes) and given
    a blocking dependency edge to this item so its conflicting axis cannot land
    first. It is to be **closed** once this item and the parent ship.
  - AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ (*F3: Instant-kind temporary windows and revert at
    expiry*) — after this change these three kinds are instant kinds for that
    item's window treatment; this item's "no effect window" and F3's
    "temporary-level TTL window" are different windows and must not be
    conflated (the effect is charge-bounded; the level has a TTL).
  - AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A (*F2: Per-upgrade temporary-window TTL in the
    catalogue*) — reads `stats.shieldDuration` / `forceFieldDuration` for timed
    kinds, so its resolver must reclassify these three (AC4).
  - AH-0MVUGI4WG008HU3M (*F5: Consumables, slots and HUD follow expiry*) — its
    AC5/AC6 premises (window countdown, slot released at window expiry) change
    for these kinds; re-read it before landing.
- **Out of scope.** Timed non-consumable kinds (Speed Boost, Frenzy, Chrono,
  Salvage, Magnet/Mineral Scoop), periodic rewards (Bomb, Smart Bomb, Orbital
  Strike) and Mystery UFO's own pickup/vacuum behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `_applyTimedEffect` cases `shield` / `thorns` /
  `force_field` become charge grants with no window; `_shieldRemaining`,
  `_thornsRemaining`, `_forceFieldRemaining` deleted or derived from the pool;
  `tryAbsorbShield` / `tryConsumeThornsRam` / `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect`
  spend through the shared pool; `thornsRechargeRemaining()` and
  `_advanceThornsRecharge` lose their "window is open" gating; module header
  rewritten.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — remove `shieldDuration`, `thornsDuration`,
  `forceFieldDuration` from the variable union, the ordered list, the specs and
  the stats type; keep the two axes per kind; update the module header and the
  temporary/permanent documentation block.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — consumable descriptions/catalogue copy for the three
  kinds, the parent's `consumable` flag, and the new
  **no-regeneration-from-pickups** property (the Q-A1=b gate) plus the
  temporary-level TTL values (15 s / 8 s / 8 s); coordinated with
  AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW and AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — drop the Thorn-specific `_powerUpRecharge` case for the
  shared consumable countdown path; assert the pickup row state.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — consumption call sites stay, but the
  armed/empty conditions read the pool (`isForceFieldActive`, thorns aura
  visibility) rather than a live window.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — bubble/aura arming follows
  "pool holds a charge"; the Shield final-second wind-down has no trigger left
  (re-point or document).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/__tests__/temporaryRevert.test.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — the window assertions per kind
  become charge assertion cycles.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (`:965`, `:974`, `:1180`, `:1189`,
  `:1190`, `:1196`, `:1205`, `:1209`) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Related work

- **Predecessor/blocker:** AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW — *Consumable upgrades should not
  be endless* (open, `plan_complete`). Supplies the shared charge pool (F2
  AH-0MVUXH0T0001N3C2), the one-event consumption/regeneration accessors (F3
  AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3), the HUD countdown (F4 AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6) and the docs
  pass (F7 AH-0MVUXH4PX0009KZR).
- **Overlap to resolve:** AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P — *Permanent Force Field should
  regenerate its reflect budget* (blocked, `intake_complete`). Same surface; its
  scope is subsumed by the parent (permanents) and this item (pickups).
- **Coordination:** AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ (*F3: Instant-kind temporary windows and
  revert at expiry*), AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A (*F2: Per-upgrade temporary-window
  TTL*), AH-0MVUGI4WG008HU3M (*F5: Consumables, slots and HUD follow expiry*).
- **Precedent:** AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT (*Per-charge recharge engine*, completed),
  AH-0MV82I8IL0012RXY (*Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence*,
  completed), AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T (*What does Field of Thorns do?*, completed —
  the Thorn aura + `next in Ns` countdown), AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (*temporary
  rather than permanent pickups*, completed), AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z (spent-dim
  bubble persistence).
- **Filed follow-up coverage:** the parent's AC8 already files this item
  (`discovered-from:AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW`, blocked by it), so intake is a
  definition pass, not a creation pass.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Balance — the drop is now much weaker (high, resolution safety-critical).**
  Under Q-A1=b a Force Field drop buys **one** reflection (today: 3–10 inside
  8–18 s) and a Thorn Field drop buys **one** ram (today: 2–6 inside 8–16 s).
  This is the producer's chosen scarcity, but it is a visible nerf to two
  popular drops and could make them read as broken in play. Mitigations: the
  granted charge **persists until used** (no window to waste), the cap axes are
  unchanged, and the change should be watched with the existing balance/eval
  harness; if it proves too weak the fix is a catalogue/level change, not a
  code change.
- **Consumable-consistency (medium).** After this change Shield / Thorn Field /
  Force Field pickups do **not** regenerate while Phase Shift / Teleport pickups
  do. That asymmetry is deliberate (Q-A1=b, scoped to the three converted
  kinds) but is exactly the sort of split that gets "normalised" by a later
  refactor, so AC4b/AC2 pin it with regression tests and the docs state the
  reason.
- **Dead-code/coupling (medium).** Retiring three catalogue axes removes the
  read path another in-flight item's TTL resolver leans on
  (AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A) and a Shield wind-down animation whose trigger
  disappears. Both must be handled explicitly (AC4, Desired change 4), not left
  as broken references.
- **HUD/slot semantics (medium).** These kinds leave the "timed window" class, so
  the F5 (AH-0MVUGI4WG008HU3M) premises around row countdown and slot release at
  window expiry no longer hold; the temporary *level* now expires on its own TTL
  while the charge persists — a combination no existing test covers today.
- **Test churn (medium).** `shieldDuration` / `thornsDuration` /
  `forceFieldDuration` appear across `effects.test.ts`,
  `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `temporaryRevert.test.ts` and `HUD.test.ts`; the
  window assertions must be rewritten as charge-cycle assertions rather than
  deleted, or the coverage for these kinds silently drops.
- **Scope creep (low).** The conversion invites "why not Frenzy/Chrono/Salvage
  too?" and "why doesn't my pickup refill?" — both deliberately out of scope
  (recorded as linked work, not expanded here).
- **Assumption A1.** A field pickup of these kinds still adds **one temporary
  level stack** (keeping today's levelling), so repeated pickups raise the cap
  for the run; the level TTL is the producer-approved flat value from the
  sibling item AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A, not a level curve (the duration axes that
  used to grow it are retired).
- **Assumption A2.** "Opens no timed window" refers to the **effect** window
  (the 8–18 s bubble/aura), not the temporary-*level* TTL; the two are distinct
  concepts and both can be true at once.
- **Assumption A3.** The HUD needs no new widget — the parent's `next in Ns`
  formatter and greyed-empty-row rules cover these kinds; this item only proves
  the pickup path reaches that state (and renders no countdown when nothing
  regenerates).
- **Assumption A6.** The Q-A1=b gate means "regenerating ceiling = cap when
  permanently owned, 0 otherwise" — a single derived number, not a second
  charge counter, and it is scoped to the three converted kinds so Phase
  Shift / Teleport pickup regeneration is untouched.
- **Assumption A7.** Because the duration axes retire, the temporary-level TTL
  is **flat** (no longer level-derived); a levelled item's temporary stack no
  longer lasts longer than a level-0 one. Recorded as an intentional
  consequence of Q-A2=a (`a` was chosen to preserve today's *level-0* window
  length).
- **Assumption A4.** A pickup grants **one** charge regardless of the resolved
  cap (the cap only bounds banking), so the conversion cannot be a stealth buff
  to a fresh pickup.
- **Assumption A5.** Checkpoint persistence is unaffected: pickup grants are
  temporary (not replayed), permanent grants are replayed — unchanged from
  today.

## Decisions (producer, 2026-10-30)

- **D1 — Q-A1 = (b): a pickup-granted charge does not regenerate.** A single
  drop buys exactly one event and the item is inert afterwards. Regeneration is
  gated on **permanent ownership** (regenerating ceiling = cap when
  `permanentGrants(id) > 0`, else 0), expressed as catalogue data, scoped to
  these three kinds so Phase Shift / Teleport pickup regeneration is unchanged.
- **D2 — Q-A2 = (a): reuse today's level-0 windows as the temporary-level TTL**
  — Shield **15 s**, Thorn Field **8 s**, Force Field **8 s**, declared flat in
  the catalogue by AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A (no longer level-derived).
- **D3 — Q-A3 = resolved: AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P is not delivered separately.**
  Re-scoped (kept open, so the requirement is not lost if the parent changes to
  drop it) with a blocking dependency edge to this item; to be closed once this
  item and the parent ship.

## Open questions

None remaining — Q-A1, Q-A2 and Q-A3 were answered by the producer on
2026-10-30 (recorded as decisions D1–D3 and in the Appendix). Two interpretation
consequences are recorded as assumptions rather than re-asked, because they
follow directly from the answers and from the code:

- **A6 (from D1).** The gate is implemented as a derived "regenerating ceiling"
  per kind (cap when permanently owned, 0 otherwise) instead of a second charge
  counter or a per-kind `id === …` branch, and it applies only to the three
  converted kinds.
- **A7 (from D2).** The temporary-level TTL is now flat rather than
  level-derived, because the duration curves it used to follow are retired.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q-A1 — Ownership/regeneration after a field pickup.**
  - Options: (a) yes — same pool and ownership as a hold-full grant (matches
    today's Phase Shift / Teleport pickups); (b) no — one charge, no
    regeneration, item inert afterwards; (c) freeform. **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): "b"** — a field pickup grants **one charge
    that is not backed by regeneration**; a single drop buys exactly one event
    and the item stays inert afterwards. Source: interactive reply. Recorded as
    **decision D1**; implementation interpretation recorded as assumption A6.
- **Q-A2 — Temporary-level TTL for the three kinds.**
  - Options: (a) reuse today's level-0 window (Shield 15 s, Thorn Field 8 s,
    Force Field 8 s); (b) uniform 15 s like the other instant kinds; (c)
    freeform. **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): "a"** — reuse the current windows. Source:
    interactive reply. Recorded as **decision D2**; the flat-TTL consequence is
    recorded as assumption A7.
- **Q-A3 — Is AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P closed or re-scoped?**
  - Asked as: *"Decide whether AH-0MVNX40F2005CM8P (Permanent Force Field
    regenerate budget) is closed or re-scoped, since its remaining scope is
    subsumed by this item."*
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-30): "yes"** — i.e. do not deliver it
    separately. Source: interactive reply. Interpreted conservatively as
    **re-scope now, close after this item and the parent ship** (D3): closing a
    still-blocked item today would lose the requirement if the parent's scope
    changes, which is the same rule the parent's plan applied to
    AH-0MV82IA9U004BOKP.
- **Q-A4 (agent, technical — answered by code evidence, no producer needed).**
  *Must the window axes be retired or merely excluded?* Answer (eng): **retired**
  — the parent's AC4 asks for no dead axes, and the three axes are read only by
  `_applyTimedEffect` for these kinds (`src/powerups/effects.ts:535/592/636`),
  so removal is contained. A `DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` exclusion stays
  as the documented fallback only if a consumer is found that cannot be removed
  in this change.
- **Q-A5 (agent, technical — answered by code evidence).** *Does the change need
  a new counter for "remaining absorptions", or a second counter for
  pickup-vs-permanent charges?* Answer (eng): **neither** — the pool count is
  the remaining budget, and D1's gate is a derived regenerating ceiling, so
  `_shieldRemaining` / `_thornsRemaining` / `_forceFieldRemaining` collapse into
  the parent's pool accessors (AC2, AC4b).

## Review notes (five mini-review stages)

1. **Completeness** — problem, users, ACs, constraints, existing state, desired
   change, key files all present; the retired-axis consumer (TTL resolver) and
   the no-regeneration gate were added as explicit ACs (AC4, AC4b) after the
   related-work pass and the producer answers.
2. **Capture fidelity** — the producer's answers are represented verbatim
   (Q-A1 = "b", Q-A2 = "a", Q-A3 = "yes") with the interpretation of each
   recorded as a named decision/assumption, including the one genuinely
   ambiguous answer (Q-A3, "yes" to "closed or re-scoped").
3. **Related-work & traceability** — parent plan children (F2/F3/F4/F7), the
   subsumed Force Field item, the three coordination siblings and the
   precedent items are referenced with ids; the automated report is retained.
4. **Risks & assumptions** — six risks with mitigations, seven assumptions;
   the balance risk flipped from "pickup becomes a slow endless pool" to "the
   drop is now much weaker", and both the consumable-consistency asymmetry and
   the scope-creep risk are recorded.
5. **Polish & handoff** — UK English, file paths with line evidence,
   copy-pasteable AC numbering, headline in one sentence.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3** – Registry one-event consumption and regeneration accessors (blocked)
- **AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ** – F3: Instant-kind temporary windows and revert at expiry (blocked)
- **AH-0MVUXFDFN009QK84** – Consumable catalogue flag and charge axes (open)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absorbed, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+139 more)
- `README.md` — matched: absorbed, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+137 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: absorbed, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+127 more)

# Goal

As a player, I want a between-sortie defence report that tells me which of my
hexes were attacked, which held and which fell, and the exact numbers behind each
result — and as a demo watcher I never want attract mode to stall on a defence or
on a new screen.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § UI / scene
  surface (the between-sortie defence report) and § Attract mode ("the bot
  traverses or skips every new screen — on the map it auto-picks the **weakest**
  adjacent hex, in the hangar it auto-buys the cheapest useful unlock, and it
  auto-advances the defence report. Because defence is resolved algorithmically,
  there is no live defence battle for the demo to stall in").
- Failure modes to mitigate: *opaque defence* ("a hex falls and the player cannot
  see why … show the numbers (defender rating vs. attacking force)") and *the
  frontier treadmill* (an answerable tick, shown).
- Today there is no scene-to-scene menu traversal in demo mode — the demo boots
  straight into `PlayScene` — so the traversal here is new behaviour
  (`src/ai/`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`).

## Scope

- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts`: per-hex rows from the resolver's per-tick
  record — attacking force, aggression, defender rating, outcome, margin, and
  what it would take to retake the hex — plus a continue action back to the map.
- Frontier tick integration: the tick runs between runs (on returning from a
  deployment) and its record feeds this screen.
- Attract-mode traversal for the whole new surface: menu → map → (weakest hex)
  deployment → defence report → map → hangar (cheapest useful unlock), driven by
  pure, tested bot decisions with seeded choices; no live defence battle exists to
  stall in.

## Tests first

Report-rendering tests from a synthetic tick record and a full traversal
integration test (bot drives every new screen without stalling) before the scene
and bot wiring.

## Key Files

- new: `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` (+ test), traversal decisions in
  `src/ai/` (+ tests)
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B3 (tick record), B5 (between-run wiring) and A5 (hangar).
- Prerequisite for timing validation (B7).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The defence report shows the numbers that produced every result: per hex the
  attacking force, aggression, defender rating, hold/fall outcome, margin and what
  it would take to retake it, generated from the resolver's per-tick record.
- **Attract mode never stalls.** The demo bot traverses or skips the map, hangar
  and defence report (auto-pick weakest hex, auto-buy cheapest useful unlock) and
  there is no live defence battle to stall in.
- An integration test drives menu → map → deployment → defence report → map →
  hangar with the bot and asserts every screen advances within a bounded time and
  no defence battle is ever simulated.
- The report is a pure view over the tick record and the stored payload — the same
  code path runs in `GymHexWar`, with no gameplay rule in the scene.

# Goal

As the producer, I want the ring's play time and playstyle trade-off measured
rather than guessed — ring 1 at 40–60 minutes and ring 2 at ≈70–100 minutes for a
semi-skilled player, with the rush line faster-but-riskier and the grind line
safer-but-slower — so the ring lands as an evening's play and neither strategy is
strictly dominant.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § Session shape
  ("the **one-ring MVP targets 40–60 minutes** … **Ring 2 is larger — 12 hexes** —
  so it lands at … **≈70–100 minutes**") and § Playstyles supported ("No style is
  strictly dominant — the aggressive line is **faster but riskier** and slow
  grinding is **safer but slower**, which is the intended trade").
- Intake assumption A1: timing is measured with the existing headless eval arena —
  `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` reports per-run `durationSeconds` / `ticksSimulated`, so
  a ring's play time is summed from simulated deployments rather than guessed. No
  new instrumentation is required.
- Intake assumption Q4: the headless arena is sufficient evidence for the
  recorded target; a human playtest is desirable but not a gate.

## Scope

- A headless ring-timing harness (a thin driver over `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) that
  simulates a ring's deployments at their resolved aggression and sums
  `durationSeconds`, plus a modelled build/retry allowance so the budget covers
  the whole ring rather than deployments alone.
- Two strategy simulations: **rush** (weapon hex first, then push into the next
  ring) and **grind** (secure the ring before pushing); record deployments,
  losses, salvage and wall-clock minutes for each.
- Tuning of aggression growth, defender ratings and grant strengths so both
  budgets and both strategies land in range; record the measured numbers,
  method and confidence in the GDD §8 timings section (B8 writes the prose; this
  item supplies the numbers) and on the work item.
- Any budget miss beyond tolerance raises a child item rather than silently
  widening the target.

## Tests first

A deterministic timing-harness test (same seed → same summed duration) and a
budget-assertion test with an explicit tolerance before tuning.

## Key Files

- new: `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` (+ test / CLI entry), ring timing fixtures
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`,
  `src/data/frontier-tuning.json`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B6 (the whole ring loop, including the between-run tick).
- Prerequisite for the docs item (B8).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Timing targets.** One-ring MVP is completable in 40–60 minutes by a
  semi-skilled player; ring 2 (12 hexes) lands at ≈70–100 minutes; the timing is
  recorded in the GDD and measured with the headless eval arena
  (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` per-run durations, summed per ring).
- **Playstyles supported.** A rush through the weapon hex into the next ring, and
  a full grind of the ring before pushing, are both viable and neither is strictly
  dominant; the difficulty curve makes the aggressive line riskier but faster.
- The timing harness is deterministic (same seed and payload → same summed
  duration, asserted by a test) and a budget test asserts both ring windows with a
  stated tolerance.
- The measured numbers, strategy comparison and method are recorded on the work
  item for the docs item to publish.

# Goal

As a player and maintainer, I want the Hangar War documented as a playable
specification and its build status recorded, so the docs of record (GDD §8,
`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `README.md`) describe what
now ships rather than what was proposed.

## Goal

Give the consumable set and its charge curves a single data home, so nothing
downstream needs an `id === …` special case and every cap/interval is tunable
from the catalogue.

Parent: AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (Consumable upgrades should not be endless).

## Desired change

- `PowerUpEntry` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) gains `consumable?: boolean`, set on
  exactly the six kinds in the agreed set: Shield, Thorn Field, Phase Shift,
  Teleport, Force Field, Mystery UFO. A derived `CONSUMABLE_POWER_UP_IDS`
  export lists them (catalogue order) and is the only place the set is spelled
  out.
- Catalogue `description` copy for those six states the charge model: one
  charge buys one event, charges regenerate on a level-derived interval, and a
  hold-full reward adds a charge rather than a level.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` gains the three new level axes from the
  parent's matrix:
  - `shieldRecharge` — seconds to regenerate one Shield charge, **45 s at
    level 0**, descending (shorter) with level;
  - `forceFieldRecharge` — seconds to regenerate one Force Field reflect,
    **45 s at level 0**, descending (shorter) with level;
  - `mysteryUfoChargeCap` — how many Mystery UFO drone charges one pool holds,
    **1 at level 0**, ascending (higher) with level.
  Each is registered in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` in catalogue order, with the
  derived `*RechargeRate` companion where the existing conventions require it,
  and surfaced on `PowerUpLevelStats`.
- No behavioural change yet: existing resolution paths are untouched, so the
  suite stays green at this point.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Parent-AC traceability (restated from AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW)

- AC-2 — *Covers parent AC2 (restated):* **AC2 — Charge caps and regeneration follow the agreed configuration.** The


- AC1 — `PowerUpEntry.consumable` exists and is `true` on exactly the six agreed
  kinds; every other catalogue entry and every weapon drop leaves it unset. A
  test asserts the exact set against `CONSUMABLE_POWER_UP_IDS`.
- AC2 — `CONSUMABLE_POWER_UP_IDS` is derived from the catalogue (not a
  hand-maintained list) and a test fails if the catalogue and the derived list
  ever disagree.
- AC3 — `shieldRecharge` resolves to 45 s at level 0 and shortens with level;
  `forceFieldRecharge` resolves to 45 s at level 0 and shortens with level;
  `mysteryUfoChargeCap` resolves to 1 at level 0 and increases with level. A
  level-0 test plus at least one levelled point per axis pins the direction.
- AC4 — The existing axis completeness and monotonicity suites
  (`powerUpLevels.test.ts`) pass with the three new axes registered.
- AC5 — Catalogue descriptions for the six kinds mention the charge/regeneration
  model, and no consumer outside the catalogue hard-codes the consumable id set.

## Constraints

- **No rebalance by stealth.** Do not change existing shipped values; the new
  axes only add the 45 s-at-level-0 curves and the level-0 cap of 1.
- **Catalogue-driven.** No magic numbers in the store, registry, HUD or scenes.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/types.ts`
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`
- `src/powerups/types.test.ts`

## Dependencies

## Goal

Generalise the shipped Phase Shift / Teleport charge engine into **one** charge
pool that serves every consumable, and make a permanent (hold-full) grant add a
charge instead of a level.

Parent: AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (Consumable upgrades should not be endless).

## Desired change

- Replace the Phase-Shift/Teleport-specific fields (`_phaseCharges`,
  `_teleportStacks`, `_phaseRechargeTimers`, `_teleportRechargeTimers`) with a
  per-kind pool: `Map<PowerUpId, number>` of available charges plus per-kind
  recharge timers, covering all six consumables.
- Public API (additive; keep the existing Phase Shift / Teleport methods as thin
  delegates so current tests and consumers keep working):
  - `consumeConsumableCharge(id)` — spends exactly one charge; returns `false`
    at zero; starts a recharge timer whose duration is the level-derived
    interval **at the moment of consumption**.
  - `consumableCharges(id)` / `consumableChargeCap(id)` /
    `consumableRechargeTime(id)` / `consumableRechargeRemaining(id)`.
  - `grantConsumableCharge(id, count)` — clamped grant used by the hold-full
    path; grants never exceed the cap and never bank while full.
- `collect(id, true)` for a consumable adds exactly one charge and **does not
  increment the permanent grant count** (so `getPermanentLevel` and
  `getEffectiveLevel` stay unchanged, which is what the hold-full pricing and
  every level consumer read). `_phasePermanent` generalises to a per-kind
  "owned" flag so an empty pool still reports ownership.
- `tickRecharge(dt)` advances every kind's timers, is frame-rate independent
  (a long frame returns as many charges as the elapsed time warrants, remainder
  carried, no banking past the cap) and remains the **only** regeneration
  driver. `reset()` clears every pool and timer.
- Field-pickup grants keep the shipped per-kind semantics for now (producer
  decision 2 / PD5); only the permanent path changes in this child.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Parent-AC traceability (restated from AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW)

- AC-1 — *Covers parent AC1 (restated):* **AC1 — Permanent grant adds a charge, never a level.** For every consumable
- AC-2 — *Covers parent AC2 (restated):* **AC2 — Charge caps and regeneration follow the agreed configuration.** The


- AC1 — For each of the six consumables, `collect(id, permanent = true)` leaves
  `getPermanentLevel(id)` and `getEffectiveLevel(id)` unchanged and increases
  `consumableCharges(id)` by exactly one. One test per kind.
- AC2 — The grant clamps at the level-derived cap: a grant on a full pool is
  discarded, and no charge is banked while the pool is full (a partially spent
  pool does not accumulate credit for the downtime). Test per kind at cap.
- AC3 — Cap and interval resolve from the catalogue: level 0 gives Shield 1 /
  45 s, Thorn Field 2 / 12 s, Phase Shift 1 / 30 s, Teleport 1 / 15 s,
  Force Field 3 / 45 s, Mystery UFO 1 / 30 s; one levelled point per kind moves
  cap and time in the documented direction.
- AC4 — `consumeConsumableCharge` spends one charge, returns `false` on an empty
  pool, and starts a timer with the level-derived duration at consumption time;
  the spend → empty → regenerate → re-use cycle is covered per kind.
- AC5 — `tickRecharge` is the only regeneration path: no charge returns without
  a tick; many small ticks and one long tick produce the same result; elapsed
  over-cap credits do not bank; `reset()` clears pools and timers.
- AC6 — The existing Phase Shift / Teleport public methods still behave exactly
  as before (their current tests pass unmodified), proving the generalisation is
  behaviour-preserving for the shipped kinds.
- AC7 — Unit tests are written first in this child (red locally, green at
  commit); no test in the repository is left failing.

## Constraints

- **Pure and deterministic.** The store stays free of scene/storage coupling so
  the game and every gym share one model.
- **No clawback.** An expiring temporary window never removes a granted charge.
- **No new pools per scene.** All six kinds live in this one store.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the catalogue/axes child (consumable set + new axes must exist).

## Goal

Make one charge buy exactly one event in the shared `EffectsRegistry`, and
expose the charge count plus regeneration countdown so the HUD can read them for

Parent: AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (Consumable upgrades should not be endless).

## Desired change

- Per-kind one-event consumption routed through the shared charge pool:
  - **Shield** — one absorbed hit consumes one charge (the permanent bubble
    stops being an endless window; it is armed only while a charge is held).
  - **Thorn Field** — one free ram consumes one charge.
  - **Force Field** — one reflected bullet consumes one charge.
  - **Mystery UFO** — one drone spawn consumes one charge.
  - **Phase Shift / Teleport** — unchanged in shape (already one event), now
    served by the shared pool.
- Existing budget accessors (`shieldAbsorptionsRemaining()`,
  `thornsRemaining()`, `forceFieldRemaining()`) project the pool for
  permanently-owned kinds, so the armed/empty visuals and the existing HUD
  stacks read the same source; temporary (field-pickup) windows keep their
  current timed behaviour and budget handling in this change (PD5).
- New registry accessors for the HUD: `consumableCharges(id)` and
  `consumableRechargeRemaining(id)` covering all six kinds (`undefined`/`0`
  semantics documented and tested).
- Regeneration advances only from the existing `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` call
  site, so the game and every gym regenerate identically. `reset()` clears it.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Parent-AC traceability (restated from AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW)

- AC-3 — *Covers parent AC3 (restated):* **AC3 — One charge = one event, no timed window.** Each kind's charge is spent


- AC1 — Shield: a permanent Shield is armed only while it holds a charge; one
  absorbed hit spends one charge; the pool then regenerates on the level-derived
  interval; there is no endless timed window for a permanent Shield.
- AC2 — Thorn Field: one free ram spends one charge; the pool regenerates on
  `thornsRecharge`; a permanent field's ram budget no longer refills endlessly
  inside a permanent window.
- AC3 — Force Field: one reflected bullet spends one charge; the pool
  regenerates on `forceFieldRecharge`; a permanent bubble dims when empty and
  re-arms when a charge returns.
- AC4 — Mystery UFO: one drone spawn spends one charge; a permanent UFO spawns
  at most `mysteryUfoChargeCap` drones per regeneration interval instead of
  spawning forever, and never exceeds the cap.
- AC5 — Phase Shift and Teleport keep their current spend/regenerate behaviour
  through the shared pool; their existing tests pass unmodified.
- AC6 — `consumableCharges(id)` and `consumableRechargeRemaining(id)` report the
  correct value for all six kinds in the states empty / partial / full
  (countdown absent when full).
- AC7 — The spend → empty → regenerate → re-use cycle is covered per kind at
  registry level, and no charge regenerates without a `tick(dt)` call.
- AC8 — Unit tests are written first in this child (red locally, green at
  commit).

## Constraints

- **Shared seams only.** No per-scene timers or consumption paths.
- **No behaviour change for field pickups** (that is AH-0MVUVSW4J0009QUW).
- **No dead axes.** Any axis this child stops reading is either still used by

- Blocked by the store charge-pool child.

## Goal

Make a field pickup of Shield, Thorn Field or Force Field grant exactly one charge of the shared consumable pool (no effect window), spend one charge per event through the existing seams, and gate regeneration on permanent ownership as catalogue data.

Parent: AH-0MVUVSW4J0009QUW (Timed consumable field pickups should use the absorbed-hit model). Predecessor: AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW (Consumable upgrades should not be endless).

## Desired change

- `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect(id, false)` for `shield` / `thorns` / `force_field` grants exactly one charge via the shared pool (`grantConsumableCharge(id, 1)`, clamped at the level-resolved cap) and opens no effect window; it still adds the one temporary level stack through `store.collect(id, false)`.
- Remove `_shieldRemaining`, `_thornsRemaining` and `_forceFieldRemaining`; derive `shieldAbsorptionsRemaining()`, `thornsRemaining()` and `forceFieldRemaining()` from `consumableCharges(id)`.
- `tryAbsorbShield`, `tryConsumeThornsRam` and `tryConsumeForceFieldReflect` spend one pool charge and resolve exactly one event, returning false at zero.
- `thornsRechargeRemaining()` and `_advanceThornsRecharge` lose their window-open gating; regeneration advances only from the shared `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` call site.
- Add a catalogue property in `src/powerups/types.ts` (beside the parent's `consumable` flag) marking a kind's regeneration as requiring permanent ownership, read by the store and registry. Scope it to these three kinds so Phase Shift and Teleport pickup regeneration is unchanged; no `id === 'shield' | 'thorns' | 'force_field'` branch outside the catalogue.
- Keep the no-clawback rule: temporary-TTL expiry never reduces already-granted charges.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — A pickup grants exactly one charge and no effect window.** A Shield field pickup grants exactly one charge and opens no effect window.
- **AC2 — One charge resolves exactly one event and a pickup charge never regenerates.**
- **AC4b — The no-regeneration gate is catalogue data, not a special case.**
- **AC6 — Checkpoint resume is unchanged and singled out.** A pickup-earned charge is not persisted on resume.
- The registry-local `_shieldRemaining`, `_thornsRemaining` and `_forceFieldRemaining` counters are removed or derived from the shared pool; one charge is spent through the existing consumption seams.
- Temporary-level TTL expiry leaves the granted charge intact (no clawback); a permanent grant replays into the same charged state.
- The gate is read from the catalogue by the store and registry with no per-kind special case, scoped so Phase Shift and Teleport pickup regeneration is unchanged.

# Test-first: pure Arc chain eligibility (red tests)

Parent: Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69) — covers
parent AC1, AC2, AC4 (pure-helper half) and AC7.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want pure unit tests that pin how the Arc chain filters its
candidate list, so the rule "auto-targeting offence picks enemies, never the
inert `asteroid` world hazard" is proven without booting a Phaser scene, and a
future AOE weapon cannot silently regress into firing on rock.

## Context

`src/utils/aoe.ts` owns the pure AOE geometry. `findNearestTarget`
(`src/utils/aoe.ts:139`) and `selectChainTargets` (`:172`) currently skip only
`alive === false`; there is no target-kind filter of any sort. The Arc chain in
`CombatScene.onAoeFired` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:721`) is built from
`this.getEnemyEntities()`, which includes asteroids, so the bolt spends itself
on rock.

This item is written **first** (TDD): its new expectations are expected to FAIL
(red) until the sibling implementation item, *Shared auto-target eligibility rule and Arc wiring*, lands. It also adds the tests for the **new shared pure
module** (`src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`) that the implementation item creates.

## Scope

1. **New shared rule tests** — `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts`:
   - `INERT_WORLD_HAZARD_ARCHETYPES` contains exactly `['asteroid']` and does
     **not** contain `lane-traffic` (which stays targetable, matching the
     Orbital Strike precedent AH-0MVU3341U001B40T).
   - `isEligibleAutoTarget(entity)` is true for a live `'scout'`, true for
     `'lane-traffic'`, true for an entity with **no** `archetype` (gym
     `TrainingTarget` / historical stubs), false for `'asteroid'`, false when
     `alive === false` (including an asteroid that is already dead).
2. **Predicate-filtered geometry tests** — extend `src/utils/aoe.test.ts`
   (`describe('findNearestTarget')`, `describe('selectChainTargets')`):
   - `findNearestTarget` with an `accepts` predicate skips a **nearer excluded**
     candidate and returns the farther eligible one.
   - No predicate supplied → legacy live-only behaviour is unchanged (existing
     tests must stay green).
   - `selectChainTargets` with an `accepts` predicate: a field
     `origin → enemy A → asteroid → enemy B` within the reach budget returns
     `[A, B]` — the excluded rock **neither absorbs nor breaks a hop**.
   - An excluded rock inside the hop budget does **not** consume a link: with
     `maxLinks = 3` and only two eligible enemies, the chain length is 2.
   - The hop **reach** limit still applies to eligible targets only; an eligible
     enemy beyond `maxHopDistance` from the previous hop is not chained.
   - No eligible candidate → `[]` (and `null` from `findNearestTarget`).
   - Determinism: equal distances resolve to the earlier candidate, exactly as
     today (the existing tie-break is not reordered by the filter).

## Out of scope

- Production code changes (implementation item owns those).
- Scene-level behaviour (sibling scene-regression test item).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts` exists and asserts the shared
  exclusion list contains only `asteroid`, that `lane-traffic` stays eligible,
  that an absent `archetype` stays eligible, and that dead entities are never
  eligible.
- **AC2** — `src/utils/aoe.test.ts` asserts a nearer excluded candidate is
  skipped by both `findNearestTarget` and `selectChainTargets`, and that a chain
  in the order `enemy → asteroid → enemy` within reach returns both enemies.
- **AC3** — `src/utils/aoe.test.ts` asserts an excluded rock inside reach does
  not consume a chain link and does not break the chain, and that the hop reach
  budget still applies to the eligible hop.
- **AC4** — Legacy behaviour is pinned: calling `findNearestTarget` /
  `selectChainTargets` **without** a predicate returns exactly what it returns
  today (live-only filtering), so other callers cannot regress.
- **AC5** — Before the implementation item lands, the new expectations fail
  (red) for the missing rule/predicate; after it lands, `src/utils/aoe.test.ts`
  and `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts` pass. Evidence recorded in the
  completion comment (red → green).
- **AC6** — Full-text-free unit gate: the changed scope (`/skill:test` changed
  scope) passes.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/targetEligibility.test.ts` (new)
- `src/utils/aoe.test.ts`
- Reference only: `src/utils/aoe.ts`, `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`
  (the existing `isOrbitalStrikeTarget` rule the new module must generalise).

## Dependencies

None (test-first item; blocks the implementation item).

# Test-first: Arc-vs-asteroid scene regression tests

Parent: Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69) — covers
parent AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 (gym half), AC5, AC6 and AC7.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want a scene-level test that proves the Arc never damages,
shatters or farms an asteroid, while the Nova, Mortar and Smart Bomb pulse are
provably unchanged — so the fix cannot silently widen or narrow the exclusion.

## Context

`CombatScene.onAoeFired` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:709`) builds the Arc
chain from `selectChainTargets(x, y, this.getEnemyEntities(), aoe.chains + 1, aoe.radius)`
and derives the damage, the along-path enemy-bullet clear, the bolt VFX and the
impact feedback from that one selection. `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`
already covers Arc dispatch, chain count, bullet clearing and a no-op on an
empty field (`:815`–`:928`) — but it has **zero** asteroid coverage today.

This item is written **first** (TDD): the new Arc-vs-asteroid expectations are
expected to FAIL (red) until the implementation item lands. The
unchanged-weapon pins are expected to be GREEN before and after.

## Scope

1. **Asteroid fixture** — add an `AsteroidStub` (extends the existing
   `StubEnemy`) that reports `archetype = 'asteroid'` and counts
   `takeDamage`/destruction/accounting calls, so "untouched" is observable.
2. **Arc never touches rock** (`src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`):
   - An asteroid **nearer the ship** than the only ship enemy: firing Arc
     damages the enemy and leaves the asteroid `alive` with zero damage calls.
   - An `enemy → asteroid → enemy` line inside the 60 px chain reach: both
     enemies take damage, the asteroid takes none, the chain length stays ≤ 3
     (`chains: 2` → primary + 2 hops).
   - A **rocks-only** field: no damage, no chain VFX (`aoeEffects` empty), no
     impact cue, and no kill accounting (no `onEnemyDestroyed` / no drop / no
     mineral or Extra Life roll) — behaviourally identical to the existing
     empty-field test at `:906`.
   - The bolt VFX path and the along-path bullet clear are derived from the
     filtered chain (no segment ends on a rock; a bullet next to a
     ship→rock segment survives, a bullet next to a ship→enemy segment is
     cleared).
3. **Unchanged-weapon pins (regression, green before and after)**:
   - Nova ring, Mortar blast and the Smart Bomb pulse still damage an
     `AsteroidStub` inside their radius (AC5).
   - An entity with **no** `archetype` (`GymWeapons`-style `TrainingTarget`) is
     still a valid Arc target (AC4 gym half).
   - Destroying an asteroid by non-Arc means still yields its mineral/Extra
     Life accounting (AC6) — pin via the existing kill seam, or assert the Arc
     path performs no kill accounting at all.

## Out of scope

- Production code changes (implementation item).
- Pure geometry tests (sibling pure-helper test item).
- Player-bullet/ram asteroid kills (already covered elsewhere; only assert
  they are untouched if cheap).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — A test asserts that with an asteroid nearer the ship than a ship
  enemy, the Arc damages the **enemy** and the asteroid keeps `alive === true`
  with zero damage/death calls. (Fails before the fix.)
- **AC2** — A test asserts an `enemy → asteroid → enemy` line inside 60 px
  damages both enemies, leaves the asteroid untouched, and does not exceed the
  unchanged link budget. (Fails before the fix.)
- **AC3** — A test asserts a rocks-only field is a full no-op: no damage, no
  chain VFX, no impact cue, no asteroid kill accounting (no mineral, no Extra
  Life roll). (Fails before the fix.)
- **AC4** — Tests assert the Arc bolt path/VFX and the along-path bullet clear
  are derived from the filtered chain (no segment terminates on a rock).
- **AC5** — Regression tests assert the Nova ring, the Mortar blast and the
  Smart Bomb pulse still damage an asteroid inside their area, and an entity
  with no `archetype` is still Arc-targetable. These pass before and after the
  change.
- **AC6** — A test asserts the Arc performs no asteroid kill accounting, while
  the shared asteroid kill path (other means) still awards its mineral/Extra
  Life behaviour.
- **AC7** — Every new test names the behaviour it pins (parent AC id in the
  test title), and the changed-scope gate (`/skill:test` changed scope) passes.
- **AC8** — Red → green evidence recorded in the completion comment.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`
- Reference only: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`

## Dependencies

None (test-first item; blocks the implementation item).

# Shared auto-target eligibility rule and Arc wiring

Parent: Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69) — covers
parent AC1, AC2, AC4, and the behaviour behind AC3.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the Arc bolt to strike the nearest **enemy**, hop across
rocks to further enemies, and do nothing at all when the field holds only rock
— so my timed weapon is spent on threats and cannot farm minerals or Extra
Lives off asteroids I never aimed at.

As a designer, I want that rule defined **once** in a pure shared module and
consumed by the shared combat core, so the game and every gym cannot drift
(gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1) — exactly as the Orbital Strike fix
(AH-0MVU3341U001B40T) did for the single-target strike.

## Context

- Arc is the only auto-targeting AOE weapon: `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.arc.aoe`
  (`trigger: 'onFire'`, `radius: 60`, `chains: 2`) is dispatched through
  `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `CombatScene.onAoeFired`
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:709`), which calls
  `selectChainTargets(x, y, this.getEnemyEntities(), aoe.chains + 1, aoe.radius)`
  and then applies damage, the along-path bullet clear, the bolt VFX and the
  impact feedback **from that one selection**.
- `src/utils/aoe.ts` filters only `alive === false`.
- `Asteroid.archetype === 'asteroid'` (`src/entities/Asteroid.ts:274`);
  `PlayScene.getEnemyEntities()` returns asteroids too.
- Precedent: `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts` already excludes the
  `asteroid` archetype (`ORBITAL_STRIKE_EXCLUDED_ARCHETYPES`) and explicitly
  notes "every other weapon may still hit asteroids".
- A destroyed **small** asteroid pays one mineral plus a roll at the
  configurable Extra Life chance, which is why the every-beat auto-chain is
  also a power farm.

## Implementation sketch (minimal end-to-end slice)

1. **New pure shared module `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`** (layering: `src/utils`
   may not import from `src/scenes`, verified):
   - `INERT_WORLD_HAZARD_ARCHETYPES = ['asteroid'] as const` — the rock hazard
     only; `lane-traffic` stays targetable.
   - `isInertWorldHazard(archetype?: string): boolean` — an **absent**
     archetype is never a hazard (gym `TrainingTarget`s and historical stubs
     stay targetable).
   - `isEligibleAutoTarget(entity)` — `alive !== false` **and** not an inert
     world hazard. Identify by archetype **string**, never `instanceof`.
2. **`src/utils/aoe.ts`** — add an optional trailing `accepts?: (target: T) => boolean`
   parameter to `findNearestTarget` and `selectChainTargets` (default:
   live-only, so existing callers and tests are byte-for-byte unaffected);
   thread it through the hop loop. Keep both helpers pure and deterministic
   (existing earlier-candidate tie-break preserved).
3. **`src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`** — delegate
   `isOrbitalStrikeTarget` / `ORBITAL_STRIKE_EXCLUDED_ARCHETYPES` to the new
   shared module, keeping both exports and their exact behaviour so the
   existing Orbital Strike tests and callers stay green. Update the module JSDoc
   to say the rule is now shared with Arc.
4. **`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`** — in `onAoeFired`, pass
   `isEligibleAutoTarget` to `selectChainTargets` so the chain, the path
   (`path`), the along-path bullet clear, `applyArcChainEffect`,
   `spawnArcChainVfx` and `resolveChainImpactFx` all describe the same
   filtered strikes. Update the JSDoc on `onAoeFired` /
   `applyArcChainEffect` and `selectChainTargets` to state the rule.
5. **No tuning, no per-scene copies**: fire rate (1 beat), radius (60 px),
   chain count (2) and the catalogue description are unchanged; the change
   lives only in shared code, so `PlayScene` and every gym (including
   `GymWeapons`, whose `TrainingTarget`s have no archetype) inherit it.

## Out of scope (linked, not folded in)

- Extending the exclusion to Nova / Mortar / the Smart Bomb pulse (parent
  Assumption A1 and Appendix Q1 — recommended: no).
- Adding a "bolt fizzles" cue when no eligible enemy exists (a silent beat is
  the existing empty-field behaviour).
- Re-tuning Arc's power budget; that belongs to Weapon upgrades are too
  powerful (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` exists, is pure (no Phaser, no
  scene import), exports the inert-hazard list plus `isInertWorldHazard` and
  `isEligibleAutoTarget`, and excludes only `asteroid`; an absent archetype is
  eligible.
- **AC2** — With an asteroid nearer the ship than a ship enemy, firing Arc
  strikes the enemy and leaves the asteroid `alive`; on an
  `enemy → asteroid → enemy` line inside 60 px both enemies take damage and the
  rock takes none (parent AC1, pinned by the sibling scene test item).
- **AC3** — A chain hop whose geometrically nearest next candidate is a rock
  continues to the next eligible enemy within the unchanged 60 px reach and the
  unchanged link budget (`chains: 2` → primary + 2 hops) (parent AC2).
- **AC4** — A field holding only asteroids is a full no-op: no damage, no chain
  VFX, no impact cue, no asteroid kill accounting — identical to the existing
  empty-field behaviour (parent AC3).
- **AC5** — The bolt path/VFX and the along-path bullet clear are derived from
  the filtered chain, so no segment is ever drawn to a rock.
- **AC6** — The rule exists in exactly one place: `CombatScene` consumes the
  shared helper, no gym or scene defines its own copy, and
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (the duplicate-body guard)
  still passes (parent AC4).
- **AC7** — `selectChainTargets` / `findNearestTarget` remain backward
  compatible: with no predicate supplied they behave exactly as before, so
  existing callers and their tests are unchanged and green.
- **AC8** — `strikeTargeting` behaviour is unchanged (its existing tests stay
  green) and the Orbital Strike rule now delegates to the shared module rather
  than duplicating the archetype list.
- **AC9** — Nova, Mortar and the Smart Bomb pulse still damage asteroids inside
  their areas; the cannon still destroys an asteroid on contact (parent AC5,
  pinned by the sibling test item).
- **AC10** — Enemy-ship scoring/drop/wave accounting is untouched, and asteroid
  rewards via other means are unchanged (parent AC6).
- **AC11** — The changed-scope gate (`/skill:test` changed scope) passes; the
  full suite passes at the dev-push gate (parent AC7, AC9).

## Key Files

- `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts` (new)
- `src/utils/aoe.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- Reference only: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/entities/Asteroid.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by both test-first items:
- Pure Arc chain eligibility (red tests)
- Arc-vs-asteroid scene regression tests

# Document the auto-target eligibility rule

Parent: Arc weapon should not affect asteroids (AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69) — covers
parent AC8.

## Goal (user story)

As a designer, I want the auto-targeting rule written down in the design docs
and in the code JSDoc, so a future AOE weapon cannot silently regress into
"fires on asteroids" and the docs never promise behaviour the code does not
deliver.

## Context

The docs currently describe Arc as "strikes the nearest enemy"
(`docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 table row A3, line 962) and
`src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts` records that "every other weapon may still
hit asteroids". After the Arc fix, that sentence is the standing rule for all
**auto-targeting** offence, so the docs need one explicit statement of scope:
auto-targeting picks enemies; aimed/area weapons may still hit rock.

## Scope

1. **`docs/Game Design Document.md`**
   - §4.4 AOE weapons table, row **A3 (Arc)**: add that asteroids are never
     targets — the chain hops across/around a rock so the link budget and the
     60 px reach are unchanged — and name the shared helper.
   - The **"AOE weapons — Nova, Mortar and Arc"** appendix paragraph
     (line ~992): add the standing rule — *auto-targeting offence targets live
     enemies only and skips the inert `asteroid` world hazard; aimed fire,
     Nova, Mortar and the Smart Bomb pulse may still hit asteroids* — plus the
     shared-module reference and the coverage line (add the new test file).
2. **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`**
   - The asteroid/world-hazard section (near the Orbital Strike / AOE notes,
     ~line 166 and the `CombatScene.onAoeFired` divergence note ~line 1710):
     state that the `asteroid` archetype is excluded from **all** auto-targeting
     offence (Arc chain + Orbital Strike), and that excluding by archetype
     string keeps it identical in the game and the gyms.
3. **`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`**
   - The `GymWeapons` row (and its divergence table entry "AOE practice
     targets"): note that the `TrainingTarget`s carry **no** `archetype`, so
     they stay valid Arc targets and the gym still visibly demonstrates the
     bolt under the new rule.
4. **Code JSDoc** — the helper module, `selectChainTargets`/`findNearestTarget`
   and `strikeTargeting.ts` each state the rule and cross-reference the parent
   item (the JSDoc text itself lands with the implementation item; this item
   verifies it is present and accurate, and fixes drift).
5. **`README.md`** — review only: it lists Arc in the drop/weapon inventories
   but makes no claim about targeting. Record in the completion comment that no
   README change was needed (or make the minimal correction if a targeting
   claim exists).

## Out of scope

- Player-facing text: the catalogue description already says "strikes the
  nearest enemy" (parent Assumption A4), so `src/utils/weapons.ts` copy needs
  no change.
- `CHANGELOG.md` (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — GDD §4.4 row A3 states that Arc never targets asteroids, that hops
  skip rock without consuming a link, and references the shared helper.
- **AC2** — The GDD AOE appendix paragraph states the standing auto-targeting
  rule, distinguishes auto-targeting from aimed/area weapons, and lists the new
  coverage test file.
- **AC3** — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` states that the
  `asteroid` archetype is excluded from auto-targeting offence (Arc + Orbital
  Strike) and why exclusion is by archetype string (gym parity).
- **AC4** — `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records that `GymWeapons`' archetype-less
  `TrainingTarget`s remain Arc-targetable, so the documented divergence still
  holds.
- **AC5** — JSDoc on the shared helper, on `selectChainTargets` /
  `findNearestTarget` and on `strikeTargeting.ts` states the rule and
  cross-references AH-0MVNSIG1O0049G69; no doc claims a behaviour the code does
  not have.
- **AC6** — `README.md` is reviewed with the outcome recorded in the completion
  comment (no stale targeting claim remains).
- **AC7** — Documentation assertions that are machine-checked
  (`src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`, any docs assertion suites) still
  pass under the changed-scope gate.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`
- `./README.md`
- Reference only: `src/utils/targetEligibility.ts`,
  `src/utils/aoe.ts`, `src/scenes/core/strikeTargeting.ts`

## Dependencies

Blocked by *Shared auto-target eligibility rule and Arc wiring* (documents the
implemented behaviour, not the intent).

## Goal

As a producer or future maintainer, I want the six-slot rules and their presentation recorded in the canonical docs, so the difference between a *slot* and a *HUD row* is discoverable and the capture-setup divergence is a written decision rather than a surprise.

## Context

The cap's semantics are already documented (GDD §4.4 "Loadout slots", `docs/BALANCING.md` "The six loadout slots") and guarded by `src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts`. RCA (AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX) found the docs never say how the HUD presents occupancy, so a player counting rows concludes the cap is broken: the HUD can show 7 rows for 5 slots (exempt Mystery UFO + residual Phase Shift/Teleport charges) and 5 rows for 6 slots (temporary one-shot kinds such as Strike render no row).

## Scope

Extend the existing sections (do not rewrite them):

- **HUD presentation:** one row per owned/active kind, but only slot-counted rows form the loadout; the slot budget readout; exempt entries marked as always-available; Phase Shift/Teleport charge rows marked as charge-only and explaining why they outlive their temporary window.
- **Row/slot discrepancy cases:** temporary one-shots (Bomb/Smart Bomb/Strike) hold a slot while active but render no row; a Teleport arrival opens a Phase Shift row for an unowned kind; Extra Life is surfaced by the lives counter.
- **Capture-setup divergence:** the decision recorded by the acquisition-surface child (`sceneSetup.ts` may pre-grant more than six kinds for gym/video scenes, never in normal play), with the reason and the guard.
- **Evidence method:** a short note that `npm run record` plus a replay against `resolveSlotState()` is how a >6 report is triaged (including the `--auto` / Ctrl+C stop requirement, cross-referenced to AH-0MVVH57LL00038WQ).
- Docs-guard tests in the style of `src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts` asserting the new statements exist and stay true (no silent drift).

## Acceptance Criteria

**Discovered from:** AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C (shared background layer). **Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1.

## Problem

Slices 1–3 deliver the deterministic level→background manifest, the 20 bundled JPEGs under `public/assets/backgrounds/` and the shared dimmed background layer — but nothing in production code ever registers those textures with Phaser's texture manager (no `load.image` / `preload` for `backgroundAssetPath`). Today `PlayScene` therefore renders the layer's solid `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` fallback and the player never sees a NASA photo, which leaves parent AC1 ("backgrounds render at the full 960×540 canvas") unmet in the shipped game.

## Goal

As a player I want each level's real NASA photo behind the gameplay, and as a developer I want the load path to be shared (game and gyms) and non-blocking, so the backdrop appears once its JPEG decodes without shifting scene boot timing or stalling `create()`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A shared loader (e.g. `loadBackgroundTextures(scene, keys)` in `src/scenes/core/` or the shared background layer) starts a Phaser file load for `backgroundAssetPath(key)` for every required key, once per scene/texture-manager lifetime, and never blocks `create()` (mirrors the lazy `MenuScene` GitHub-logo load pattern).
2. On load completion the live background layer re-renders with the decoded texture (upgrading from the fallback) without leaking listeners or re-loading an already-present key on scene restart.
3. Load failure (404/decode error) keeps the solid `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` fallback and does not throw; the failure is observable (single warning) but not fatal.
4. `PlayScene` and the gym path (per the gym-parity decision in AH-0MVSEC0J0004YNJC) consume the same loader; no forked copies (duplicate-body guard passes).
5. Tests: with `public/assets/backgrounds/` mocked/registered, booting `PlayScene` eventually shows the level-1 photo after the load completes; the deterministic boot stays deterministic (fixture-based tests keep the fallback until a fixture is registered); load failure path tested.
6. `npm run build` and the full suite pass.

## Rationale for a separate item

The epic's seven-slice plan did not assign runtime image loading to any slice (slice 2 bundled the files, slice 3 built the layer against injected fixture textures, slice 5 wires level changes, slice 6 gym parity). This was found during slice 3 implementation; it is a prerequisite for parent AC1 in the shipped game.

data.comment:
Implementation approach (fresh session after the drive reset discarded the previous WIP).

**Why the previous attempt died:** the worktree was reset because `finish` reported a build failure three times. Re-checked here: `npm run build-audio` exits 0 (the ToneForge sibling-revision line is a *warning*, not a failure), so the recorded message was the last stderr line of a genuine TypeScript failure in the discarded WIP, not an environment blocker.

**Design**

- New `src/scenes/core/backgroundLoader.ts` — `loadBackgroundTextures(scene, keys, options)`: queues `scene.load.image(key, backgroundAssetPath(key))` for keys the texture manager lacks, then `load.start()`; returns the queued keys synchronously (never blocks `create()`), mirroring the lazy `MenuScene` GitHub-mark pattern.
- **Once per texture-manager lifetime:** requested keys are tracked in a `WeakMap` keyed on `scene.textures`, so a scene restart never re-requests a key the game already holds (or already failed to fetch).
- **Upgrade in place (AC2):** the shared `BackgroundLayer.setLevel` calls the loader whenever the level's texture is missing and re-applies the level from the loader's `filecomplete` callback, so the live layer upgrades fallback → photo. Handlers are detached as soon as every requested key settles, and on scene SHUTDOWN/DESTROY.
- **Failure path (AC3):** a `loaderror` keeps the solid `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` fallback, warns exactly once for that key and does not throw.
- **Shared, not forked (AC4):** the loader is reached *through* the shared layer, so `PlayScene` and every `CombatScene` gym consume it by construction via `_createBackground`/`_setBackgroundLevel`; no scene-local load code exists. The gym enable/disable decision stays with AH-0MVSEC0J0004YNJC (still `intake_complete`) — whichever way it goes, the gym gets this loader through the same hook, and the duplicate-body guard needs no allow-list entry.
- **Determinism (AC5):** under Vitest (`MODE === 'test'`) the default asset source is never fetched, so scene suites keep the fallback until a fixture is registered (same convention as `configStore`'s test-mode I/O gate). Loader tests inject a data-URI source (`resolveSource`) and exercise the real Phaser load path offline; `createBackgroundLayer` takes an optional test-only source override.

**Tests:** new `src/scenes/core/backgroundLoader.test.ts` (request-once, skip existing, non-blocking return, live-layer upgrade, no reload on restart, failure keeps fallback + single warning, no network in tests) and an added no-network assertion in `src/scenes/PlayScene.background.test.ts`.
